items.statement: Management reaffirmed target to double revenue in 3 years from today
items.quote: Faisal Hawa: And we do stand by our statement of doubling revenue in 3 years from today. Shishir Joshipura

items.statement: Order backlog as of September 2024 stands at Rs 41.5 billion with 72% domestic orders
items.quote: The order backlog as of September '24 is at 41.5 billion comprising of 72% of domestic orders.

items.statement: Order intake in Q2 FY25 was Rs 9.21 billion with 94% from domestic market
items.quote: The order intake during the quarter was 9.21 billion with 94% from the domestic market.

items.statement: Government lifted restrictions on cane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production
items.quote: On the domestic bioenergy business front, in a much-awaited development, the government lifted restrictions on use of cane juice, cane syrup and B-heavy molasses for Ethanol production.

items.statement: Food Ministry approached NITI Aayog to prepare roadmap for 25% ethanol blending
items.quote: With a target of 20% ethanol blending with petrol on track, the Food Ministry has approached the NITI Aayog to prepare a roadmap for 25% blending.

items.statement: Brazil legislated Fuel of Future law increasing ethanol blending to 30% from 27%, creating 4 billion liters additional demand
items.quote: Brazil has legislated Fuel of the Future law that will increase the default blending to 30% up from 27% currently. This is expected to create a demand for an additional 4 billion liters of Ethanol.

items.statement: Additional 3-3.5 billion liters annual capacity needed to achieve 25% blending from current 20% target
items.quote: Roughly 3 to 3.5 billion liters annual capacity would be required to be built to meet this additional 5%.

items.statement: R&D CAPEX expected to reach Rs 65-70 crores by end of FY25 including lactic acid plant capitalization
items.quote: By the end of this year, we should have CAPEX of almost on the R&D side itself around 65 to 70 crores.

items.statement: GenX Mangalore facility lease capitalized under Ind AS, adding Rs 22 crores depreciation in H1 FY25
items.quote: If you look at for last six months, our depreciation was in a range of 18 crores, but if you look at for the half year, it has translated into 40 crores, so almost 22 crores increase on account of that depreciation which is mainly coming up because of this GenX facility which we have put up.

items.statement: Q2 margins sustainable going forward with variation due to sales mix and engineering services execution
items.quote: I think the quarter 2 margins should keep on continuing on a sustainable basis. Of course, on a quarter on a quarter basis, you will see some kind of a variation happening for the reason to what extent we are executing the engineering services order, which are not the services business segment which we are mentioning. And second one is the sales mix mainly on the domestic and international. So, to

items.statement: 100% of Q2 FY25 bioenergy order book from starchy feedstock, predominantly maize
items.quote: Capacity built up in this quarter was completely dominated by starchy feedstock, with 100% share of our order book being from starchy feedstocks for this segment.

items.statement: Commissioned demo biopolymer facility with 100 TPA lactic acid, 60 TPA lactide, 55 TPA PLA capacity
items.value: 100 tons per annum for Lactic Acid, 60 tons per annum for Lactide, which is equal to 55 tons per annum of PLA
items.quote: This integrated facility houses fermentation, chemical synthesis, separation and purification sections along with other supporting sections and is spread over 3 acres. This facility showcases production capacities of 100 tons per annum for Lactic Acid, 60 tons per annum for Lactide, which is equal to 55 tons per annum of PLA.

items.statement: Commissioned corn oil demo plant at customer site producing 4 tons per day for biodiesel feedstock
items.quote: We have commissioned a demo plant for production of corn oil at one of our customers' installations. Corn oil is one of the by-products at the corn-based ethanol plants. This plant can produce 4 tons per day of corn oil.

items.statement: IOCL 2G plant recommissioning progressing as planned with gradual ramp-up
items.quote: On 2G front, IOCL plant recommissioning progress is as per plan. We are working closely with the IOCL team to ensure ramping up of the plant capacity in gradual manner.

items.statement: GenX Mangalore facility approvals received from 4 leading global EPC companies, revenue expected from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have already received the approvals from four of the leading global EPC companies. As the process of approval and then discussing new orders itself is long, we have not seen any major order booking for Praj GenX, though the inquiries are building up meaningfully.

items.statement: Services order book for H1 FY25 is 40% higher than full FY24 order book
items.quote: Our order book for H1 of FY '25 is 40% higher than our order book for the entire last year for this segment.

items.statement: Export revenue accounted for 27% of Q2 FY25 revenue
items.quote: Export revenue accounted for 27% of Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: MTM loss of Rs 10 crores on forward contracts in Q2 FY25 due to euro movement, reversed in October
items.quote: Oh, yes, the total quantum on this MTM losses was 10 crores.

items.statement: Cash in hand as of September 30, 2024 is Rs 7.51 billion
items.quote: Cash in hand as on 30th September '24 is 7.51 billion.

items.statement: Supreme Court judgment on state taxation powers applies only to industrial alcohol, not ethanol for blending
items.quote: No, that is specifically as it relates to industrial alcohol and is more a question as to who has authority between the state and the centre and has no impact at all.

items.statement: Praj has clear value proposition in Latin America starchy feedstock markets with 3 corn ethanol plants under engineering
items.quote: As you are aware, we have already commissioned a plant, we are engineering for three more, and I am sure that as we go forward, we will probably hear about further developments in these markets as well.

items.statement: US SAF target of 3 billion gallons by 2030, with ~1 billion gallons via ATJ route requiring 20 projects of 100M gallons each
items.quote: United States has said that the target is to put 3 billion gallon s capacity for SAF, okay. Roughly, I am just putting for ease of calculation now, 2 billion, 1.6 to 2 billion will come through the HEFA route. And after that everything will likely to come through, at least in the near future likely to come through the ATJ route. So, let us take up to 2030, it is a billion gallons of ethanol to be

items.statement: Praj addresses 40-50% of CAPEX for ATJ SAF plants, ~$400M potential per project
items.quote: Almost, it depends on the scope, of course, of what we can address, what we can, there are other dimensions as well, but between 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Ethanol producers awaiting price revisions; indicative grain price from FCI very high challenging project viability
items.quote: The ethanol producers are also awaiting price revisions for ethanol. The grain-based distilleries are now allowed to purchase up to 2.3 million metric tons of rice from FCI exclusively for ethanol production. However, the indicative grain price is very high, posing a big challenge on project viability.

items.statement: Cellulosic feedstock supply chain needs organization for farm-to-factory logistics
items.quote: What is of importance is that we establish the correct supply chain for this and that needs to get organized. I think that is one area where we definitely need to work on that w e need to organize ourselves as an industry

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to resource addition in Praj GenX subsidiary, services business and annual increments
items.quote: Increase in the employee cost is because of addition of resources in our subsidiary called Praj GenX, and services business and normal annual increments.

items.statement: Biogenic CO2 capture emerging as significant services opportunity with concentrated global movement
items.quote: Additionally, we are also seeing a big move happening globally on capture of biogenic CO2. There is a CO2 that gets released in the fermentation process. And we expect that this could become a significant product line as we move forward.

items.statement: Plans ~$20M investment over next 6 quarters to expand sales network in US and Europe; products ready, focus now on go-to-market
items.quote: next 6 quarters, we should be spending around… we still have to work out the details on the investment, which will be close to $20 million. We are in the board meeting we were discussing about it that it's an opportunity. It's the lowest cost investment because the products are

items.statement: Total costs stable QoQ (INR 477 cr vs 483 cr); may rise to INR 495-500 cr with sales investments; revenue increase to INR 650-675 cr would expand EBITDA significantly
items.quote: Our costs are now stabilised. Last year and last quarter was 483 Crs. This time it's 477 Crs. So, the total cost is 6 Crs lesser than the last quarter. It may go maybe 495 to 500.

items.statement: AI deals face significant regulatory influence; contracting teams taking time to address new AI regulations before signing
items.quote: AI is going through a significant amount of regulatory influence, with new regulations coming in. So, even the contracting teams do take time to put together all their signatures before they go ahead with us

items.statement: Revenue mix: 39% USD, 18% GBP, 16% INR, 7% EUR, 6% CAD, 14% other currencies
items.quote: 39% of our revenues are in USD followed by 18% in GBP, 16% in INR, 7% in Euro, 6% in CAD and 14% from other currencies.

items.statement: Received Gold Award for continuous learning culture; Most Preferred Workplace for Women Award 2024-25
items.quote: We have received the Gold Award for excellence in creating a culture of continuous learning and up skilling at The Economic Times Human Capital Awards. Secondly, we have been honoured with the Most Preferred Workplace for Women Award 2024-25

items.statement: Order book stands at INR62 crores after securing INR26 crore order for switchyard construction and INR3.4 crore refurbishment contract
items.quote: First, we secured an order worth of INR26 crores, which brings our total order book to INR62 crores.

items.statement: Expects stronger H2 FY25 with revenue growth exceeding 10% YoY as clients take delivery before March closing
items.quote: We are expecting more than that. Since the second half, generally, the production and demand and pressure will be more.

items.statement: New 6-acre facility with INR70-75 crore investment to be operational by December 2025, 20-30% construction complete
items.quote: The project represents INR70 crores to INR75 crore s investment and has a potential to generate revenue of INR500 crores to INR550 crores at full

items.statement: New plant will increase production capacity to 9,000 MVA per year, focused on 25-160 MVA, 110-230 kV power transformers
items.quote: This is the state -of-the-art plant, which will significantly increase our production capacity to 9 ,000 MVA per year, helping us better meet the rising market demand.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 77 bps to 20.53% in H1 FY25; product margins average 10-12% across segments
items.quote: Our EBITDA came at INR12.03 crores with a margin of 20.53 percentage, reflecting an improvement of 77 basis points.

items.statement: Strong demand for power transformers above 50 MVA and 110 kV; distribution transformer demand exists but competitive with 40-50 manufacturers in Tamil Nadu
items.quote: The current demand is for transformers which are above 230 KV and above 50 MVA. And for this type of power transformers only, there is a big demand.

items.statement: Revenue split: 60% power transformers, 40% distribution transformers; solar/wind (IDT) now 10%+ of sales vs <5% last year
items.quote: As of now, on our total sale, last year it was less than 5%. Now, we are reaching 10% on overall sale and 10% and above.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute 70-80% of revenue; reduced government utility exposure to <14% from TANGEDCO/TANTRANSCO, focusing on private IPPs
items.quote: And the government exposure for the last half year is less than 14%. And the non-government is around 86%.

items.statement: Receivables well controlled; high March receivables collected, >50% of current FY receivables already received
items.quote: And for the current financial is applied also, we have almost more than half the thing we have received. So, the receivables are well under the control.

items.statement: Exports <2-3% to Africa; targeting North America market after new facility operational, no commitments yet
items.quote: Currently, we did expor t, but it's not significantly high, maybe less than 2 % to 3% for African countries. Now, we are planning to expand as we are seeing a good market in North America.

items.statement: Power transformer realization INR10-12 lakh/MVA; distribution transformer INR20-22 lakh/MVA; CRGO steel supply challenging but managed via vendor relationships
items.quote: For power transformer, it will be like 11 lakhs to 12 lakhs per MVA. And for distribution transformers, it will be around 20 lakhs to 22 lakhs per MVA.

items.statement: SNR from Hyderabad main competitor in renewable transformers; Indotech focused on larger transformers, fully booked, giving Supreme delivery advantage
items.quote: SNR. SNR from Hyderabad, I think it is not a listed company and they are doing good.

items.statement: Order inflow pipeline >INR100 crores; bidding win rate 10-20%; substation works order INR12 crore with 2-3 more expected at INR10-30 crore each
items.quote: Bidding pipeline is very high. It is more than INR100 crores, and very recently we have posted a tender in NLC, Neyveli Lignite Corporation.

items.statement: Current plant utilization 30-50%; limited to 25 MVA/110 kV; new plant needed for >25 MVA transformers
items.quote: Current plant utilization is around 30% to 50%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth 10-30% YoY from new plant (operational only 3 months in FY26); substation inquiries start February 2025 for FY26
items.quote: FY '26, the same like 10% to 30% will be the increase on the revenue side growth. Actually, the new plant will be commissioned or will come to completion in the month of December '25 only.

items.statement: CRGO steel supply challenging; no domestic manufacturer; managing through 20-30 year vendor relationships
items.quote: Yes. Now we are seeing a challenge in getting CRGO from the market. And though we have 20, 30 years relationship with our vendors and we are able to manage the supply demand.

items.statement: CPRI certification required for larger transformers; stage-by-stage qualification for government tenders; no import restrictions except duty
items.quote: And for going forward, going for a bigger type of transformers, we have to get certification from CPRI. That is the Central Power Research Institute to validate our design.

items.statement: One large order delayed ~1 month (INR4-5 crore impact) due to client-side payment/dispatch clearance issues; recurring pattern with 10% of customers
items.quote: That is for about INR4 crores-INR5 crores. Something around INR4 crores-INR5 crores. Yes.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin of 26.7% for Q2 FY25, highest ever quarterly margin
items.quote: The reported EBITDA margin stood at 26.7% for the quarter, which is our highest ever quarterly EBITDA margin that's reported by Cipla.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 maintained at 24.5% to 25.5%
items.quote: The overall company outlook, we are on track to achieve our margin guidance for the year. That is between 24.5%, 25.5%.

items.statement: One India business grew 5% YoY; acute category slow due to anti-infectives market growth at 4.9% vs 12% last year
items.quote: On an overall basis, One India growth stood at 5% year-on-year. Our endeavor is to outpace the market growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: Chronic therapies outperformed market: respiratory 9%, cardiac 11%, urology 15%; chronic share improved to 61.5%
items.quote: Our branded prescription business continued to outpace market growth in chronic therapies. Respiratory grew by 9%, cardiac grew by 11, and urology by 15%. Our share of chronic also improved to 61.5% as per IQVIA MAT September '24.

items.statement: Added three new brands in Rs 100 crore+ revenue category; total 25 such brands and 21 in top 300 per IQVIA
items.quote: In our branded prescription business, we have added three new brands in the category of revenue of over Rs. 100 crores. We now have a total of 25 brands in this category, along with 2 1 brands in top 300, as per IQVIA MAT September '24.

items.statement: Consumer Health business grew 20%+; anchor brands Nicotex, Omnigel, Cipladine maintained leadership
items.quote: the coming quarters. Our Consumer Health business witnessed strong traction with anchor in transition brands continuing to grow bigger. The business posted a robust growth of 20% plus

items.statement: North America revenue $237 million; Albuterol market share 19%, Lanreotide franchise 35% per IQVIA MAT-24
items.quote: In North America, we delivered a quarterly revenue of $237 million. Barring a temporary supply issue in Lanreotide, the sustenance in revenue has been supported by continued positive traction in our differentiated portfolio.

items.statement: Lanreotide supply issues due to partner capacity reconfiguration and higher demand; Q3 sales expected lower than Q2, recovery from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Currently, we are facing some supply challenges in Lanreotide, and hence we expect the Quarter 3 Lanreotide franchise sales to be lower than quarter 2. However, these issues are anticipated to be resolved by the end of Quarter 3, and starting quarter four FY25, we should be able to recover sharply in the Lanreotide franchise.

items.statement: Partner investing in Lanreotide capacity expansion; Cipla investing in MDI facility at Fall River for new filings and de-risking
items.quote: We're also working to increase the overall capacity of Lanreotide through CAPEX investments made by our partner.

items.statement: One Africa business grew 22%; South Africa private market secondary growth 8.6% vs market 0.5%, now rank 2 in private market
items.quote: Our overall One Africa business recorded a vigorous growth of 22% with South Africa also delivering a similar growth in local currency terms. In the private market, our secondary growth was at a healthy 8.6% versus the market growth of 0.5%.

items.statement: EMEU business grew 18% in USD terms with pickup in DTM and B2B categories
items.quote: In EMEU, our deep market strategy has started paying off with the business delivering a solid growth of 18% in US dollar terms, with a pickup in both our DTM and B2B categories.

items.statement: Goa facility received six 483 observations from US FDA re-inspection; classification awaited; Indore remediation ongoing
items.quote: Our Goa facility recently underwent re-inspection by the US FDA. The facility was issued six 483 observations. We are still waiting for the classification of the inspection. At Indore, our focus remains on remediation and implementation of the CAPA.

items.statement: Generic Advair de-risking on track for H1 FY26 launch; generic Abraxane likely from Goa facility pending approval, CMO route as backup
items.quote: De-risking of generic Advair, our major inhalation asset, has been progressing as per expectations. We expect to launch this asset in the half -one of FY 26. For generic Abraxane, while we are more likely to launch it from our Goa facility, this may require approval for the facility, impacting the timeline of the launch.

items.statement: Gross margin 67.6%, up 159 bps YoY driven by better mix; API costs moderated but propellant and freight costs increased
items.quote: The reported gross margin after material costs stood at 67.6% for the quarter which is 159 basis points above last year's figures, mainly driven by overall better mix.

items.statement: China plant operations commenced, expected to start supplies in FY25; added 1,500+ field force in India branded prescription between FY23 and H1 FY25
items.quote: It also includes commencement of our plant operations in China, which is expected to start supplies in this financial year itself, and investment in our MDI facility in Fall River for filing new products and de-risking some of our existing pipelines.

items.statement: Debt including lease liabilities Rs 461 crore; net cash Rs 7,950 crore as of September 2024; paid Rs 1,000+ crore dividend this quarter
items.quote: As at September 2024, a debt on our balance sheet including the lease liabilities stood at Rs. 461 crore with net cash equivalent balance of Rs. 7950 crore. This quarter we had paid out a dividend of Rs. 1000 plus crore.

items.statement: Dividend payout near 30% target; buyback under active board discussion; M&A focus on India domestic formulations and US differentiated injectables
items.quote: We have talked about 30% dividend payout. We are already close to that and with the improvement in profits, that should continue to go up. Buyback is a matter of discussion at our board.

items.statement: R&D spend Rs 385 crore (5.5% of revenue), up 2% YoY; new focus areas: oligonucleotides, peptides, respiratory assets, bio asset moving to phase 1
items.quote: R&D investments for the quarter are at Rs. 385 crore or 5.5% of the revenue, driven by product filing costs and developmental efforts higher in the quarter by 2% versus last year.

items.statement: US price erosion ~10% YoY blended, 3-5% QoQ; Albuterol seeing some erosion from competition
items.quote: So YoY is about 10% on a blended basis overall. S o that's on an average basis. Qo Q is a low single digit, so about 3% to 5% roughly.

items.statement: US base business erosion low double digits (~10%) in oral solids and government supplies; differentiated portfolio 70% of US sales
items.quote: So, 70% would be more differentiated assets for us.

items.statement: Symbicort, Qvar, and partner inhaled asset filings timeline unchanged at FY27
items.quote: So the timeline has not changed for us. So the guidance that we had given earlier that of FY27, that continues to be there for Symbicort and Qvar, and one more partner inhaled asset that we have talked about.

items.statement: Participating in semaglutide generic opportunity in India; in-licensing GLP-1 drugs from MNCs an option
items.quote: Yes, Sema generic we will be participating and I think hopefully we will be amongst the first wave of people to enter in India. In-licensing is always an option for us in deepening our partnership with large multinational corporations that sell categories of GLP-1 drugs.

items.statement: Goa facility classification timeline uncertain; committed corrective actions over 6-12 months; FDA follow-up questions answered
items.quote: So the timelines we have committed to the FDA with over the next six months to a year perspective from aspects that we have determined are important, but those are, I think the classification of the inspection by the FDA, that data is awaited from the FDA.

items.statement: Lanreotide partner facility is multi-product; production equipment dedicated to product category; expansion primarily for Lanreotide line
items.quote: No, the facility is multi -product. I think the production equipment is dedicated to us or to the category of product, let me put it that way.

items.statement: Sustainability: S&P Dow Jones Sustainability Index score improved to 79 from 70 previous year
items.quote: During the quarter, Cipla achieved ranking with the S&P Dow Jones Sustainability Indices, and the score has improved to 79 from 70 that was there in the previous year.

items.statement: Revised revenue potential guidance for FY27 lowered to INR3,500-4,000 crores from earlier INR4,200-4,500 crores due to current API pricing levels
items.quote: So we would like to revise it down because of the current API prices. So what we feel that -- now I think that the current potential will be anywhere between INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores as far as current pricing levels are concerned.

items.statement: Standalone business potential revenue of INR2,750 crores at current pricing and capacity excluding greenfield projects
items.quote: But I can give you one indication that with current pricing level and our current capacit y, it will roughly give now a potential revenue of around INR2,750 crores on a stand- alone business, which will include both API and spec chem

items.statement: FY25 sales expected to be flattish versus FY24 due to negative rate variance and lacklustre demand in first half
items.quote: So we feel that this FY '25 might look flattish by the end of the entire FY '25 versus FY '24.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 15-15.5% as efficiencies return and renewable energy reduces power costs
items.quote: So with all those efficiencies back in place, we feel that we should be targeting around 15% to 15.5% EBITDA in the long term.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 11.5%, anticipating improvement by end of FY25 driven by selling price upturn and export demand growth
items.quote: stood at INR68.5 crores with EBITDA margin at 11.5%. PAT stood at INR35 crores. Going away by the end of FY '25, we anticipate an improvement in margins, mostly driven by upturn in selling price levels and an anticipated demand growth in export sales

items.statement: Q2 YoY negative rate variance of 7-8% in API segment; QoQ variance minimal at -0.5%; prices stabilizing at composite level but some antibiotic/antifungal products still declining
items.quote: Y-o-Y basis, we have seen around 7%, 8% negative rate variance for the quarter 2. For the quarter 1, it was a little higher. But now as quarter-on-quarter, the rate variance is hardly 0.5% at a composite level.

items.statement: Salicylic Acid prices dropped from INR150-160/kg to INR125-130/kg due to Chinese dumping; salicylate derivatives now more attractive
items.quote: Earlier, the prices were at the level of INR150 to INR160 per kg. It has now come down to INR125 to INR130. But because of the fall, now the salicylates are looking more attractive.

items.statement: Export demand showing uptick with increased inquiries; domestic demand stable per Harit Shah; election-related export slowdown in H1 easing
items.quote: So now the export demand should come back. We have already seen a little bit of uptick in the number of inquiries as far as the export markets are concerned.

items.statement: Salicylic Acid production at ~100 tons/month, targeting 300+ tons/month by end of Q3 FY25; total capacity 1,800 tons/month to ramp through FY25-26
items.quote: Currently, we are producing roughly around 100 tons per month. There have been certain teething issues and we expect to ramp up the production to 300-plus tons per month by the end of the current quarter.

items.statement: Metformin capacity at 1,350-1,400 tons/month, targeting 1,700-1,800 tons/month short-term; long-term visibility of 2,000-3,000 tons/month with adjacent land parcel
items.quote: So right now, we do have a capacity of around 1,350 to 1,400 tons per month in between. So the plan was to scale it up to 1,700 to 1,800 in a very short term.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex ~INR90 crores; full year FY25 capex guidance ~INR200 crores funded by internal accruals and term loans
items.quote: During H1 FY '25, the company has incurred capex of approximately INR90 crores, mainly towards capacity expansion and the greenfield projects, backward integration and new product launches. anticipate a total capex of roughly around INR200 crores for the full year.

items.statement: CWIP of ~INR300 crores expected to capitalize by Q3 FY25 (max Q4) as Sayakha greenfield project comes online
items.quote: Roughly. Mostly Q3 itself, if not then, at max Q4, but this year itself.

items.statement: Formulation export order book >$12 million; Q2 formulation exports only $2-2.5 million due to US FDA and UK MHRA audits at Baddi plant
items.quote: we have a very strong order book of around more than $12 million for the formulation bus iness. So the export potential is very much there, we have a lot of orders in hand

items.statement: US FDA audit in September 2024 resulted in 7 observations (no repeats); CAPA response submitted within 15 days; US FDA approval received for oncology block at Baddi; UK MHRA approval for OSD facility
items.quote: We got 7 observations, but we see we are q uite confident about the observation. In fact, in the closing meeting we did ask him, what they feel about the API facility. So he was like, it is like any other API facility, any other API facility

items.statement: US FDA resolution expected to improve European market access first; meaningful US sales impact unlikely in first 6 months post-resolution
items.quote: Before even the US business kicks in, our European business also will show some signs of improvement from that particular plant. So first 3 months, I don't expect anything that, frankly speaking. Next 3 months, that is from out to 6 months, probably some approvals -- more approvals will be on the way.

items.statement: API therapeutic mix: antibiotics 40%, antidiabetic 18%, antiprotozoal 17%, anti-inflammatory 10%, antifungal 10%, others 4%; Formulation exports 53% of segment revenue
items.quote: For the quarter gone by within the API business, the antibiotic therapeutic category contributed approximately 40%, antidiabetic around 18%, antiprotozoal around 17%, anti-inflammatory around 10%, antifungal around 10% and rest contributed around 4% to the total API sales.

items.statement: Completed buyback of 665,000 equity shares at INR900/share in September 2024; committed to maintaining shareholder payouts while investing in growth
items.quote: In September 2024, the company has completed the buyback of 665,000 equity shares at a price of INR900 per share. Face value of INR10 each fully paid up in September 2024.

items.statement: Salicylic Acid plant ramp-up delayed by steaming issues causing ~INR5.5 crores PBT impact in Q2; Derma facility suboptimal (~INR200 crores capex) targeting breakeven by November
items.quote: In fact, even this quarter, I would point out that around INR5.5 crores impact was there at the bottom line just because you can say we are not able to absorb those increased overheads because of the lower production and the potential.

items.statement: Published first sustainability report; committed to reducing carbon footprint despite leading API manufacturing capacity
items.quote: This was the first year where we had published our sustainability report. It is published on our website. Please have a look at it because we strive to reduce our carbon footprint in spite of having the leading capacity in manufacturing sector of API industry.

items.statement: Board approved 1:1 bonus issue and stock split from INR10 to INR5 face value pending shareholder approval
items.quote: In celebration of Linc's 30th anniversary, our Board has approved a 1-1 bonus issue and a stock split, subdividing each equity share with a face value of INR10 into two shares with a face value of INR5, pending shareholder approval.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue CAGR target of 17% to 20%
items.quote: Looking forward, we are confident in achieving our projected medium-term revenue growth of 17% to 20% CAGR, driven by well-aligned strategic initiatives and robust business fundamentals.

items.statement: Pentonic brand recorded 24% growth in Q2 FY25
items.quote: with Pentonic leading the charge and recording a robust 24% growth in Q2.

items.statement: Gross profit margin improved to 31.8% in Q2 FY25 driven by favourable product mix
items.quote: Our gross profit margin improved to 31.8%, driven by a favourable product mix shift led by Pentonic's strong performance.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin was 11.9% in Q2 FY25, up 29.5% year-on-year
items.quote: Operating EBITDA experienced significant growth, increasing by 29.5% year-over-year to INR169 lakhs, with an operating EBITDA margin of 11.9%.

items.statement: PAT margin increased to 6.4% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: PAT also improved by 14% year -on-year, reaching INR879 lakhs and achieving a PAT margin of 6.4%.

items.statement: Launched three new Pentonic pens at INR20, INR30, INR40 with nationwide rollout underway
items.quote: in the recent few months, we have launched three new pens at price points of INR20, INR30 and INR40 in select markets, with a nationwide rollout underway.

items.statement: Entering mechanical pencil category under Linc and Pentonic brands in H2 FY25
items.quote: Additionally, we are making our entry into the mechanical pencil category, with launches under both the Linc and Pentonic brands in the second half of this fiscal.

items.statement: Planning Pentonic-branded mathematical drawing instrument launch in Q4 FY25 and markers test launch in same quarter

items.statement: Demand growth guidance for FY25 at 4-5% with H2 expected at 8-9%

items.statement: Cost reduction target of INR 450-500 per ton by March 2028, 25-30% achieved so far

items.statement: Full year FY25 organic capex guidance of INR 7,000-8,000 crores
items.quote: So closer to INR7,000 – 8000 crores, is what we are expecting for the full year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex of INR 3,500 crores incurred, on track for full year target
items.quote: I think we have already done close to INR3,500 -odd crores for the first half, well on track.

items.statement: 4 million ton clinker and 6.4 million ton cement capacity to commence by Q4 FY25, taking total to 100+ million tons

items.statement: 115 million tons capacity by Q3 FY26, 118 million tons by end FY26, 140 million tons by FY28

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition adds 8.5 million tons, post-completion capacity 97.4 million tons

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 14.8%, EBITDA per ton INR 780; H1 FY25 margin 15.1%, EBITDA per ton INR 795
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR 1,111 crores at a margin of 14.8% and EBITDA per ton of INR 780.

items.statement: Operational cost per ton declined 4% YoY to INR 4,497; energy cost down 10%, kiln fuel cost down 13%, freight down 7%
items.quote: On the operational cost for the quarter, it was INR4,497 per ton, showing a decline of 4%.

items.statement: Green power share increased to 18.2% from 15.6%, AFR share to 9.5% from 7%; targeting 60% green power by FY26
items.quote: The share of AFR and fuel mix has improved to 9.5% from 7%. The share of Green Power and fuel mix has increased from 15.6% to 18.2%.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost reduced 10% to INR 1,276 per ton; logistics cost reduced 7% to INR 1,282 per ton
items.quote: Driven by better fuel management and structure initiatives undertaken, our power and fuel costs have decreased by 10% to INR1,276 per ton in quarter 2 FY '25 from INR1,425 per ton in quarter 2 FY '24.

items.statement: 70 million tons limestone reserves secured in Q2 FY25 via two new mine wins in MP and Maharashtra
items.quote: To secure our limestone supplies in quarter 2 FY '25, we have won bids for another 2 new mines having reserves of 70 million tons, 1 in Madhya Pradesh and 1 in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Targeting 218 MW WHRS by March 2025, currently 196 MW; 1,000 MW RE by FY26, 200 MW Khavda phase 1 charged
items.value: 218 MW WHRS by Mar 25, 1,000 MW RE by FY26

Currently, the WH RS capacity is 196 megawatts. We have earlier announced our investments in 1,000 megawatt of RE, which is expected to get commissioned by FY '26.

items.statement: Organic volume growth of 5-5.5% YoY excluding acquisitions; consolidated volume growth 9% YoY
items.quote: We would still be around 5%, 5.5%, Raashi.

items.statement: Premium products share in trade sales up 300 bps to 26%; blended cement at 84%; direct dispatch up 600 bps to 55%
items.quote: blended cement at 84%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales by 300 bps up to 26%.

items.statement: Secondary lead distance reduced 7 km to 47 km; primary lead distance 271 km vs 272 km
items.quote: Primary lead distance i n the current quarter was in 271 versus 272, and secondary lead distance at 47 versus 54.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with AAA rating; cash and equivalents INR 10,135 crores as of Sep 30
items.quote: Needless to highlight Ambuja remains debt-free, and we are in the highest bracket of all the ratings in terms of AAAs.

items.statement: Warrants program brought INR 8,300 crores in April 2024
items.quote: Then in April, the warrants program gave another INR8,300-odd crores.

items.statement: Binding agreement to acquire 46.8% stake in Orient Cement; acquisition via internal accruals
items.quote: Ambuja enters into a binding agreement to acquire 46.8% stake in Orient Cements Limited. The acquisition complements existing cement footprint, reducing overall lead distance and logistics costs and improving market share in core markets.

items.statement: Penna integration progressing well: 70-75% clinker utilization in 45 days, targeting 80-85% in 3 years now expected sooner
items.quote: During our acquisition, we had given targets to hit 80%, 85% in, say, 3 years' time, but I see that we wi ll be able to achieve much before that.

items.statement: Sanghi plant: one kiln refurbished and running, second kiln under maintenance; marine expansion and jetty approvals underway
items.quote: In fact, almost for 2 weeks, the plant was flooded. Post that, what we have done is we have 2 kilns there, 1 kiln is fully refurbished, restarted, and now it is running the new kiln, the line 2 kiln is now fully running at free capacity.

items.statement: Net working capital outflow INR 4,000 crores in H1 due to higher receivables (OPC sales), higher coal inventory (65-70 days), lower payables
items.quote: changes in the NWC, net working capital close to INR4,000-odd crores.

items.statement: Market share ~15%, internal target 20% by FY28
items.quote: Adani Cement market share is about 15% with an internal target of 20% by FY '28.

items.statement: MSA volume ~3.7 million tons in Q2 FY25
items.quote: So our total MSA volume would be around 3.7 million.

items.statement: West Bengal incentives: INR 138 crores accrued in Q2 (Supreme Court win); FY25 run-rate ~INR 600-650 crores
items.quote: Quarterly, my incentives ballpark is around INR250-odd crores. And therefore, if I extrapolate so for a year, we're close to around, I would say, INR600 crores to INR650-odd crores is my incentives which I put in a year.

items.statement: Heavy monsoon caused 2-week flooding at Sanghi plant; solar project at Khavda delayed 2 months due to rains
items.quote: We had a very severe monsoon and impact of that was very severe in Mundra area. In fact, almost for 2 weeks, the plant was flooded.

name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited

items.statement: FY25 distillery revenue guidance of INR 1,800 crores maintained; full 700 KLPD capacity utilization expected
items.quote: See, the numbers I usually give are conservative in nature. I will stick to my 1800 figure because sometimes there's a shutdown that might be needed for any repair or overhaul. So, I'd still stick with my 1800 figure.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue around INR 2,500 crores and 8% operating margin indicated based on H1 run-rate
items.quote: Yes, as per the past two quarters here.

items.statement: 75 KLPD biodiesel plant at Bathinda targeting commissioning in April-May 2025
items.quote: Biodiesel, as I mentioned, we are targeting for April. It could go on until May of next calendar year.

items.statement: 150 KLPD ethanol expansion at Bathinda expected 12 months after order placement, targeted for November 2024 order finalization
items.quote: So, 150 once the order is placed, which, we're hoping to finalize that in the month of November. So, 12 months from there on.

items.statement: 250 KLPD ethanol plant at acquired Goyal Distillery (Fatehabad) with conservative timeline of FY28 commissioning
items.quote: For 250KL PD as for distillery, we're saying, financial year 2027-2028.

items.statement: Svaksha Distillery 100 KLPD addition reached full utilization; combined capacity now 700 KLPD
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that the recently added 100 KLPD capacity at Svaksha Distillery has reached full utilization and operations are running as planned.

items.statement: Biogas plant of 20 metric tons per day planned at Fatehabad using 250 metric tons paddy straw daily
items.quote: With the 250 LLPD ethanol, the company is planning to set up a biogas plant with a capacity of 20 metric tons per day on the newly acquired nine-acre plot near its Fatehabad unit.

items.statement: Initial ethanol order book allocation of 18.25 crore liters (~INR 1,300 crores); may increase during year based on OMC requirements
items.quote: So the total allocation we have is about INR18.25 crores. So, this should be around INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: Distillery EBITDA margin dip attributed to higher maize prices; Q3 margins expected to be maintained at Q2 levels, not increase
items.quote: See, we don't expect the margins to increase from the previous ones, previous quarter. We're hoping to maintain the same, but more clarity will be done once the crop is in.

items.statement: Biodiesel vertical integration expected to increase overall business margins once commissioned
items.quote: The overall margins of the business should increase once biodiesel has come in.

items.statement: Q2 average maize procurement cost INR 24-25/kg using wet maize advantage; current prices higher but correction expected post-Diwali
items.quote: I think the average for the quarter could be anywhere close to rupees between INR24 to INR25.

items.statement: ENA realizations INR 71-72/liter; ethanol prices same across Punjab and Kharagpur plants
items.quote: ENA prices are hovering around between INR71 to INR72. And ENA prices are also -- sorry ethanol prices are, of course, the same in both the states.

items.statement: Wet maize procurement advantage in Punjab with in-house dryers; flexible to switch between maize and rice based on profitability
items.quote: We have our own dryers in place. We were the only ethanol-based buyer for this wet maize in the market, and we anticipated very competitive rates.

items.statement: Power cost per liter: Bathinda INR 3-4 (paddy straw), Kharagpur INR 5-6; all distillery power produced in-house
items.quote: In Bathinda, we calculate this as around INR3 to INR4 only, whereas the industry standards are anywhere close to INR6 to INR7. For our Kharagpur unit, it's a little more than that. I'd say it's around INR5 to INR6 rupees.

items.statement: Bathinda: 400 KLPD with 200 KLPD ENA flexibility; Kharagpur: 300 KLPD with 200 KLPD ENA flexibility; new 150 KLPD and 250 KLPD are ethanol-only
items.quote: So, Bhatinda out of the 400 KLPD, there is flexibility to produce 200 KLPD of ENA. And for Kharagpur, that is a 300 KLPD plant, but we have the flexibility to produce up to 200 KLPD of ENA there as well.

items.statement: Ethanol sold entirely to OMCs; ENA sold to bottlers with some captive consumption for own country liquor brand
items.quote: No, ethanol is not using anything for captive consumption. It's all being sold to the OMCs, and the ENA is being sold to the bottlers, and some is being consumed by us for our own bottling purposes.

items.statement: Country liquor brand sold 8,52,241 boxes in H1 FY25; robust demand expected to continue
items.quote: BCL's country liquor brand has shown robust demand with 8,52,241 boxes sold in the first half of 2025, a trend that is expected to continue.

items.statement: Working capital loan decreased ~INR 90 crores in Q2 due to no major harvest; edible oil exit to reduce requirement by ~INR 3 crores
items.quote: Actually, this quarter, there was no big harvest happening. The only big harvest that happened was in Punjab. So, we were not sitting on a huge pile of raw material. Hence, the decrease in the working capital.

items.statement: Finance cost decreased INR 5-6 crores in Q2 due to interest subvention fund receipt; timing varies quarterly
items.quote: Yes, so the decrease was because we had received our interest subvention funds. So there's usually a quarter or two delay, we received them.

items.statement: Funding for 250 KLPD Fatehabad plant and biogas project under exploration; no decision yet on internal accruals vs debt
items.quote: For that also, currently, options are being explored, and I can give you more clarity in the future.

items.statement: Acquired Goyal Distillery Private Limited (Fatehabad) as wholly-owned subsidiary with land and permissions for 250 KLPD ethanol plant
items.quote: BCL has recently acquired Goyal Distillery Private Limited, which is located in Fatehabad, Haryana, possessing the necessary land and permissions for establishing 250 KLPD grain-based ethanol units.

items.statement: Real estate inventory being gradually sold with proceeds directed toward debt reduction
items.quote: Additionally, the existing real estate inventory is being gradually sold off with proceeds directed towards debt reduction.

items.statement: Stock exchange recategorization from edible oil to distillery segment in progress; slow process underway
items.quote: We are working on it. It's a slow process. It is in our knowledge. So, let's see how long it takes for that to be updated.

items.statement: Edible oil exit to complete by Q1 FY26 latest; revenue will decrease but profitability not expected to drop significantly due to low margins
items.quote: You know, by quarter one of financial year at the latest.

items.statement: Maize price correction expected post-Diwali from MP, Rajasthan, Jharkhand harvest but not huge decrease; prices to remain similar to Q1-Q2 levels
items.quote: Yes, but even if it decreases, we don't expect a huge decrease. So, it should be similar from Q1 numbers or Q2 numbers of this financial year.

items.statement: Ethanol volumes grew 73% YoY to 50,914 KL in Q2; distillery revenue up 95% YoY to INR 362 crores
items.quote: The distillery segment demonstrated robust growth with ethanol volumes growing by 73% to 50,914 KL. Revenue from the ethanol segment reached INR 362 crores, a remarkable 95% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Plywood volume growth guidance maintained at 8-10% for full year FY25
items.quote: We would like to maintain our guidance of 8% to 10% growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: MDF revenue growth guidance maintained at 50% year-on-year for FY25
items.quote: However, we are likely to achieve our overall rev enue growth guidance of 50% year-on-year

items.quote: we would like to maintain the full year guidance of 16% plus margins.

items.statement: Closing net debt guidance maintained at INR450 crores for FY25
items.quote: Hence, we maintain our guidance of INR450 crores as the closing debt for the year.

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 9% vs 8.5% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 9% as compared to 8.5% in quarter 2 FY '24.

items.statement: Plywood core EBITDA margin improved to 8.3% in Q2 FY25 from 7.6% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: Our core EBITDA margin for the plywood business for Q2 FY '25 was 8.3% as against 7.6% in quarter 2 FY '24.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin declined to 11.8% in Q2 FY25 from 16.6% in Q1 FY25 due to shutdown and cost pressures
items.quote: our EBITDA margins declined to 11.8% as against 16.6% in the previous quarter, which is attributable to the following reasons:

items.statement: MDF margins expected to bounce back to slightly better than 16% in Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: So quarter 3, quarter 4, we'll bounce back to the guidance what we gave around 16% for the full year. And so for quarter 3 and 4, we are assuming that our margins would be slightly better than 16%.

items.statement: New plywood plant on drawing board; decision pending due to capital allocation caution
items.quote: But then as I think we mentioned in the last call also that we are now planning to set up another plant. We are just on the drawing board, and we're doing our homework, and we'll have to come back to you people with the news of setting up of a new plant and new facility.

items.statement: Furniture fittings JV Phase 1 manufacturing to start from November 2024 after machine arrival in October
items.quote: These machines, however, have arrived at the plant in the month of October and trial runs so far have been successfully completed. We are almost now ready to start the entire Phase 1 product range manufacturing from November '24.

items.statement: BIS norms expected to restrict MDF imports and support price increases
items.quote: I think by the time the import problems starts getting -- the container issue starts getting solved, hopefully, the BIS will kick in. And because of that, people will be scared, and the volumes will be tapered.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt at INR347 crores optically lower due to INR70 crores LC for imported RM; LCs to mature by March 2025
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our net debt levels are at INR347 crores, which are optically at a lower level as we had undertaken a one-off large procurement of certain imported raw materials against LC. The impact we estimate is to be around INR70 crores for the same. These LCs are likely to mature by March '25.

items.statement: Furniture fittings JV targets INR400-500 crores revenue in next 3 years as best case
items.quote: In the next 3 years, possibly, we would be looking at anything around INR400 crores to INR500 crores as a best-case number.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected to remain challenging through FY25; easing expected from calendar year 2026
items.quote: Our team is very optimistic that starting calendar year '26, the raw material prices will start to ease. So we'll have to wait and see. Their estimate is that, yes, the whole of FY '25 still ca n remain challenging

items.statement: Inventory levels in plywood and MDF to increase in H2 to prepare for Q1 and Q2 next year
items.quote: Second, in any case, look, the inventory levels, both in plywood and MDF will also go up. So because we normally increase the inventory levels to prepare for our quarter 1 and 2.

items.statement: One-time increase in employee costs at MDF due to increments impacted Q2 margins
items.quote: the onetime increase in employee costs at the time of increments.

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited

items.statement: Targets net Stage 3 below 2% and gross NPA 4-5% by end of FY25
items.quote: If it all goes according to plan, we hope to end the year ending March '25, that is this financial year, with a net Stage 3 of less than 2%, which is substantially lower to the current 5. 38%.

items.statement: Targets 15% AUM growth in FY25 versus previous year
items.quote: As far as the business is concerned, we'll be ending the year with approximately more or less on 15% growth in AUM compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Targets debt-to-equity of 3.5x to 4x by FY27
items.quote: by FY '27, we'll be a t debt to equity of 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Aims to keep NIM above 4% and post-tax ROA around 2.5% in medium term
items.quote: Our endeavor would be to keep it upwards of 4%. That would be the levels, so that we are conscious about this and going forward in the medium term we are anywhere close to a 2.5% post-tax return on asset.

items.statement: Expects YTD disbursements to more than double by end of Q3 FY25 from H1 level of INR566 cr
items.quote: The end of quarter 3, this figure of INR566 crores would have more than doubled when we come to the end of December quarter.

items.statement: Gross NPA declined 32% YoY in value terms as of Q2 FY25
items.quote: compared to last year's September quarter, in this year's September quarter, our gross NPA has declined by 32% in value terms.

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio improved to 63-64% from 49% a year ago
items.quote: Today, our provision coverage ratio is around 63%, 64%, which is a significant layer compared to the same period last year, then it was about 49%.

items.statement: Targets gross NPA reduction of at least 50% (to INR380 cr) and ideally 75% (to INR190 cr) by end of March 2025 from INR764 cr
items.quote: Currently, if you look at it, if you have gone through our presentation, around INR764 crores was the amount in gross NPA as of September. The target- we would like to bring it down from at least by minimum 50%, ideally by 75% by end of March.

items.statement: Expects realization from NSL (INR125 cr fully provided) to be greater than or equal to INR125 cr
items.quote: Greater than or equal to INR125 crores.

items.statement: No book value reduction expected from resolution of IL&FS, Vento, Danu accounts; any appreciation to reflect in other income
items.quote: We don't expect any book value reduction. The accretion, we are not able to quantify at this point of time. Let the event happen, then we will share it with you.

items.statement: Appraised projects over INR2,100 cr at various stages of consideration as of Q2 FY25
items.quote: till date, we have appraised projects more than INR2,100 crores, which are at various stages of consideration.

items.statement: Loan book tilted toward public sector; aims to increase private sector share over medium term
items.quote: Today, of course, the loan book is tilted in favour of the public sector. So obviously, over the medium term, we will want to correct it.

items.statement: Plans to diversify borrowing: target 60% bank / 40% bonds & other sources by 2030 as ratings improve
items.quote: The intent is in the long term, say, by 2030, our borrowing from banks should come down to 60% or so, with 40% from bonds and other sources.

items.statement: Will invest in employee skill upgradation and automation to build institutional capabilities
items.quote: we'll be investing a lot in the skill upgradation, giving them greater opportunity so that by unleashing the passion of the employees and the team, we'll be able to achieve whatever we intend to do so.

items.statement: Shifting from individual-dependent to institutional capabilities via ethics, collaboration, ownership (E-C-O) culture and role rotation
items.quote: In short, what we are focusing on is how do we transition from an organization that is dependent on individual capabilities, to creating a culture where institutional capabilities are getting built.

items.statement: Resolution of large-ticket stressed assets is lumpy; outcome dependent on NCLT processes and counter-challenges
items.quote: See, these are all large ticket infra projects. So the resolution would be lumpy. We are putting in all efforts.

items.statement: Energy storage solutions are long-term trends; results may manifest over 5-10 years, not 1-2 years
items.quote: But I must caution, that when these energy storage solutions become mature, the results would manifest over a 5-10-year period. It's not like in the next 1 -2 years, this would become like a significant opportunity.

items.statement: Foundit cash burn to reduce further in Q3 and reach break-even by Q4 exit
items.quote: Last full financial year, we had a cash burn of about INR 56 crores and this year by H1 we are in a range of about INR16 crores to INR17 crores. And as we enter Q3, it should further come down and exit of Q4 is when I think we will definitely be in a break-even state.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin to inch towards 4% in H2 FY25 from current 3.8%
items.quote: So combination of these factors give us better margins in Q3 and Q4 and hence we are hopeful that from the present 3.8% margin levels that we are reporting right now, we should inch towards 4% as we move into H2.

items.statement: Demerger process on track; targeting completion by Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are hopeful of completing the entire demerger process by Q1 of next financial year.

items.statement: General staffing headcount addition slower in Q2 due to delayed festive hiring season starting mid-September vs typical August
items.quote: The pace of headcount addition was slower, mainly because of delay in festivity season hiring in Q2. Typically, the season starts in August, but this time, we witnessed that the season picked up in mid of September.

items.statement: IT staffing headwinds continue but GCC hiring supports growth; 74% of new mandates from GCCs
items.quote: Headwinds in IT/ITeS sector continued in Q2. To an extent, it affected our hirings as well. However, we reported a growth of net addition of 240 that was supported by GCCs.

items.statement: Overseas staffing muted due to Singapore visa restrictions; Middle East shows strong growth
items.quote: In terms of overseas staffing, we experienced a muted quarter mainly because of our largest market, Singapore, is undergoing headwinds due to visa restrictions that is affecting our headcount growth.

items.statement: WFM EBITDA margin at 2.44%, down 18 bps YoY due to Singapore wage inflation, general staffing mix increase to 84%, and demerger-related investments
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, EBITDA margin has contracted by 18 basis points to 2.44%, due to muted growth in Singapore market, wage inflation and increase in general staffing revenue mix, which stands at 84% from 82% a year ago.

items.statement: GTS EBITDA margin at 17.5%, within 17-18% target range; focus on international CLM growth and non-voice margin improvement
items.quote: GTS achieved a revenue growth of 2% sequentially and 7% on a year-on-year basis with an EBITDA margin for the quarter at 17.5% comfortably within our target range between 17% to 18%.

items.statement: OAM margin at 4.84%, down 14 bps YoY due to sales/leadership investments; improved 4 bps QoQ from sales penetration and margin-accretive F&B and telecom infra growth
items.quote: Operating margin for the quarter is at 4.84%, declining 14 basis points on a year-on-year basis, due to investments towards sales and leadership while it improved 4 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: WFM headcount at 498,000 including 40,000 on notice period; added 15,000 associates in Q2; general staffing 70% gross additions from Tier 2+ cities
items.quote: The platform headcount grew to 4,98,000 with around 15,000 associates added during the quarter. This includes approximately 40,000 employees who are serving notice period.

items.statement: Consolidated headcount crossed 6 lakh milestone; added 42,000 in H1 FY25 vs 56,000 in full FY24; closed H1 at 609,000 employees
items.quote: We added 42,000 in headcount and closed H1 with about 6,09,000 employees on rolls. Our net addition rate of 42,000 in first half of this year is significantly higher than the net addition of 56,000 that we added in entire FY24.

items.statement: WFM long-term margin north star at 3%; medium-term target back to 2.6-2.65%; general staffing at 1.9-2%, India IT at 9%+ (record high), international at 4.5% (down from 6.5%)
items.quote: Our WFM long-term margin trajectory north star remains at 3%. We have not moved away from that north star, but that's a long-term target for us. Where do we want to get into the medium term is back to the 2.6%, 2.65%.

items.statement: General staffing revenue mix increased to 84% from 82% YoY; IT staffing GCC contribution 68% of revenue but 74% of new business; niche/higher margin profiles now 15% of IT headcount vs <3% pre-COVID
items.quote: The general staffing business which hovers between the 1.9%-2% margin, the international business which erstwhile about a year ago prior to the regulatory and visa tightness in Singapore, internationally used to contribute between 6% to 7% EBITDA margin and India which used to again contribute between the 6% to 7% for professional staffing.

items.statement: WFM at 2.44% margin beating industry averages by 2x at 50% higher headcount and revenue; nearest competitors at half the margin rates
items.quote: At 2.44%, we are slightly softer by about 15 -20 basis points against our medium-term last co uple of quarters at about 2.6%. Having said that, the business as large as 84% contribution coming from the general staffing India business at 2.44% margin, we are already beating industry averages by at least 2x

items.statement: Government employment-linked incentive (ELI) scheme guidelines expected shortly after industry consultations; no impact in H1 numbers; benefits expected once rules finalized
items.quote: The employment-led incentive schemes as announced by the government in July have undergone a massive amount of consultation. We have participated as industry leaders and as part of industry bodies with the government at various levels in various forums.

items.statement: DSO days flat QoQ (1 day increase) and flat March-September; OCF to EBITDA conversion at 86% in H1; operating cash flow up 78% YoY to INR 245 crores
items.quote: Our operating cash flow improved 78% year-on-year to INR 245 crores with operating OCF to EBITDA conversion at 86% on a half year basis.

items.statement: Gross debt at INR 253 crores (lowest ever); repaid INR 117 crores in H1; net cash position INR 334 crores, up 142% YoY
items.value: INR 253 cr gross debt; INR 117 cr repaid; INR 334 cr net cash
items.quote: As of H1 FY 25, gross debt stands at INR 253 crores. We repaid INR 117 crores in H1 FY 25. Net cash position stands at INR 334 crores, improving 142% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Foundit: 11% revenue growth; 9 lakh job postings (highest ever); 90% candidate CSAT; 25M active users (6 months); profile updates up 61% YoY; job postings up 141% YoY

items.statement: OAM: Telecom active infra highest-ever quarterly revenue from 4G/5G network development; F&B improved as educational institutions resumed
items.quote: The Telecom active infrastructure business recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue experiencing significant growth to the development of 4G and 5G networks by the telecom operators.
