items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 450 bps YoY to 15.1% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter grew by 61% on a year-on-year basis to Rs.156 crores with EBITDA margin of 15.1%, an increase of approximately 450 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 200 bps YoY to 13.7%
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 fiscal year '25 grew by 33% to Rs.283 crores with an EBITDA margin of 13.7%, an increase of approximately 200 basis points.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by softening raw material prices, cost control, price increases accepted by market, and operating leverage
items.quote: We saw improvements in our EBITDA margin on account of softening of the raw material prices, adoption of various cost-saving measures at various plants and operating leverage, which has played due to improved volume.

items.statement: Company able to negotiate price increases with customers order-on-order basis and pass on commodity cost increases
items.quote: There has been some softening of raw-material prices, especially in the steel and we are being able to -- order-on-order basis, to negotiate the prices with our customers and pass-on the increases.

items.statement: Management believes current EBITDA margin levels are sustainable in near future
items.quote: Yes, we believe that they are sustainable.

items.statement: Strong demand across domestic segments including water, irrigation, power, oil & gas, marine & defense, industry, building & construction
items.quote: We're seeing good demand coming in and good requirement -- inquiry funnel for water as well as irrigation. The Company is making, again, a very large number of big pumps.

items.statement: International demand: UK/Europe stable with AMP8 water program opportunity, US slow due to elections, data centers slower, Southeast Asia mixed, South Africa recovering
items.quote: The UK and European market is, as you know, is not the most buoyant market, but we have developed different kinds of businesses where we've made progress. One is the services business and the other is the water business.

items.statement: UK services revenue growing from 30% to high 30s percentage of UK turnover
items.quote: normally only declare the service revenue for the UK and we've said that it's been growing from 30 and closing on to now the high 30s percentages in the UK turnover.

items.statement: Operationalized high-pressure molding lines at Dewas factory for captive casting production
items.quote: operationalization of high -pressure molding lines at our Dewas factory and operational efficiency improvements in Ki rloskarvadi Factory have contributed to this growth

items.statement: Launched indigenously manufactured submersible turbine pump for fuel stations and 13 new small pump models for dewatering, solar, water transfer
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched a new product, the indigenously manufactured submersible turbine pump for fuel station applications and 13 new models for our small pump business for dewatering, solar and water transfer applications.

items.statement: Kirloskar Ebara order book healthy at Rs.300-350 crores, new traction in fertilizer, bio-refinery, cross-country pipeline projects
items.quote: Order book is quite healthy. It's around -- it's between, I believe between just say around Rs.300 crores and Rs.350 crores.

items.statement: Developing primary heat transfer pumps for 800MW nuclear reactors, already made main boiler feed pumps for fleet reactors
items.quote: we're in the process of developing the primary heat transfer pumps for the 800-megawatt nuclear reactors. We've through -- along with Kirloskar Ebara already made the main boiler feed pumps for 800 megawatt for the fleet reactors.

items.statement: Receivables reduced from Rs.470 crores in March to Rs.303 crores in September due to strong collections from Q4 spike
items.quote: If you would have seen, there is typically a spike in our sales, especially in quarter 4 and the receivables drop is mainly all the collections which were from the March quarter and the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Provisions of Rs.20 crores in H1 for IndAS ECL on long-drawn project receivables, money safe but delayed
items.quote: These provisions are part of the normal IndAS ECL provisioning which we typically do on our project sector. So wherever we have a long -drawn project where the execution and commissioning is also involved.

items.statement: Employee cost optimization through multi-skilling, automation, younger management grooming, and internal software for time routing across facilities
items.quote: We have also deployed a system which we've developed internally for our software system for managing the times and routing times across our facilities. And this has also helped us get a better picture of the actual requirement of various people, people across different tasks within the factory.

items.statement: AP-OEM model converted made-to-order to made-to-stock for better working capital, quicker delivery, no long credit terms, dealers pay upfront
items.quote: Actually, the AP -OEM business used to be made to order and the -- and it has been converted to made to stock, because the objective is that if it's possible to move made to order into made to stock, then there is better working capital cycles and probably we can also support the customer with quicker delivery.

items.statement: KBL and SPP together possibly largest fire-fighting pump company globally with FM-approved multi-stage multi-outlet pumps
items.quote: We -- as you know, KBL and SPP have multi -stage multi-outlet pumps, which are the only ones in the world that are approved by Factory Mutual. So, there is a global demand for these products.

items.statement: US revenue delayed due to election uncertainty, customers deferring decisions, confusion may persist post-election
items.quote: A lot of finalizations were delayed and are still delayed and a lot of jobs are being deferred by customers in terms of delayed deliveries. I don't think that they don't want it, they are just moving a little slower during this election time.

items.statement: Thailand volatility due to project-based revenue without strong distribution/service baseline, unlike UK/US/South Africa
items.quote: In Southeast Asia, we're still building that li ke we've been saying and the traction was a little slower than expected, but that really causes volatility for us because then when big projects go out, it causes the revenue to move up and down.

items.statement: Kirloskar Ebara oil & gas supply chain challenges continue due to EIL-approved vendor restrictions, global monopolistic suppliers
items.quote: Those challenges will continue to be there for oil and gas, because we are restricted with the kind of suppliers that we can use. So, those continue to be there and those will be there globally, because all of these are monopolistic global suppliers.

items.statement: Other income jump to Rs.14 crores in Q2 and Rs.30 crores in H1 from treasury income due to improved cash and investment position
items.quote: This is essentially our treasury income. As you can see in our investor presentation, we have now a significant improvement in our current investment and the cash position.

items.statement: UK AMP8 water program targets 88 billion pounds spend 2025-2030 focused on clean water, KBL has over 80% market share in clear-water pumps
items.quote: The government has allocated 88 billion pounds for AMP8 and different companies are announcing what investment they're going to be doing. This includes pipelines, it includes underground pipelines, all kinds of things, but the objective of AMP8 really is movement and distribution and treatment of clear-water as against dirty water.

items.statement: New solar products expected to visibly impact revenue by Q4 FY25
items.quote: This expansion and added value should visibly impact our revenue by the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Total capex reached ~40-50 crore; additional 10-15 crore planned for FY25
items.quote: This year, our capex will be around 10 crores more, possibly adding 10 -15 crores.

items.statement: DC fast charger capacity ~1,000 units/month at ~60% utilisation; new facility operational before Jan 2025
items.quote: Currently, our capacity for DC fast chargers is about 1,000 units per month, and we are utilizing approximately 60%.

items.statement: Order book over INR 600 crore, split 70% EV / 30% solar; target mix 60-40
items.quote: As far as the ord er book is concerned, I believe we currently have over INR 600 crore in hand

items.statement: EBITDA margin improving despite falling product prices; focus on cost reduction via technology not price hikes
items.quote: When our EBITDA was 3 years ago, the price of the product was 3 times more. The product which sells for INR 4,00,000 to INR 5,00,000 today, At that time it was sold for INR 15,00,000.

items.statement: 72% of raw material by value is Indian-made; target 90%; semiconductors still imported mainly from China
items.quote: For Servotech, 72% of the raw material used to manufacture our chargers is Indian, made in India, correct? Amit Kumar: Yes. Raman Bhatia: And we will take this to 90

items.statement: Exports ~INR 40 crore last year (sampling); ~INR 10 crore in H1 FY25; targeting 40-50 countries
items.quote: Last year, the exports were around INR 40 crore; I'm not stating the exact figure, but it's approximately that amount.

items.statement: Launched Hybrid & Micro Inverters, Energy Storage Systems, Solar Pump Controllers; targeting PM Surya Ghar, C&I, distribution
items.quote: We are delighted to report notable advancements with the success ful launch of our latest range of Solar Inverters (including Hybrid and Micro Inverters range), Energy Storage Systems and Solar Pump Controllers.

items.statement: Secured big DC fast charger orders from all major oil marketing companies and auto OEMs
items.quote: We have successfully secured big orders for DC Fast Chargers from all major oil marketing companies and different different OEMs of automobile.

items.statement: New EV charging policy (Sept 18) lacks clarity; states creating nodal agencies; premature to comment on impact
items.quote: When a new policy is announced, it often requires time to be shaped into a clear framework and execution plan.

items.statement: Infrastructure bottlenecks (DISCOM connections, site readiness) limit installation of supplied chargers; may affect Q3
items.quote: Currently, we are lacking in infrastructure, meaning tha t customers, whether they are HPCL or BPCL, are not receiving the installation support they need for the materials we supply

items.statement: New manufacturing facility to be fully operational before January 2025
items.quote: The new manufacturing facility will be fully operational before January 2025.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue INR 312 crore; Q2 revenue INR 200 crore (+131% YoY); EBITDA INR 19.29 crore (+223% YoY); PAT INR 11.24 crore (+260% YoY)
items.quote: Our total income for the quarter rea ched a robust INR 200 crores representing a substantial growth of 131.1% compared to the same quarter of FY 2023 -24.

items.statement: Incorporated subsidiary for cricket team in Kolkata; driven by founder's son's passion and desire to create opportunities
items.quote: Sir, there is a reason behind everything we do, and the reason is significant—it's my son. My son is passionate about playing cricket and wants to achieve something in it.

items.statement: Focus on innovation and user experience rather than market share; aim to set own benchmarks
items.quote: If you get intoxicated and , Create your own benchmark through your thought process, and if you beat your own benchmark, then people start following you.

items.statement: Raw material cost inflation mitigated by technology-driven cost reduction; not reliant on price pass-through
items.quote: We focus on technology to minimize the impact of increased costs of raw materials for a particular company.

items.statement: Supplied systems not yet installed due to infrastructure gaps; inventory buildup risk if production outpaces installation
items.quote: This means that the systems we've provided have not yet been installed.

items.statement: Strong demand from EV mission and solar schemes; rising EV popularity and charging infrastructure needs driving growth
items.quote: The rising popularity of EVs and the increasing demand for robust charging infrastructure has been key d rivers of our growth.

items.statement: AMC revenue expected to become significant in next 3 years as installed base grows
items.quote: Currently, we don't have an AMC business, but after the projects we are executing, you will see a significant chunk of AMC in our balance sheets in the next three years.

items.statement: Total capex spent ~INR 40-50 crore; additional INR 10-15 crore planned this year; not EV-dedicated
items.quote: इस साल में िमारा क ै पेक्स हकतना ि िायेगा, ि क ै पेक्स िै र्व लगभग INR 10 कर ड़ और एड ि गा इसमें INR 10 से INR 15 कर ड़ अभी और एड ि गा।

items.statement: Net margin single-digit; focus on cost reduction via technology not pass-through; EBITDA improved over 4 years as product cost fell from ~INR 15L to ~INR 4-5L
items.quote: आि ि INR 4,00,000 से INR 5,00,000 का हबकता िै, र्वि उस समय INR 15,00,000 का हबकता था। इसका मतलब िै हक उत्पाि की लागत कम ि गई िै। त EBITDA बढ रिा िै।

items.statement: Target volume CAGR of 15-20% for next five years
items.quote: As I've told you, our target volume, compound annual growth would be around 15% to 20% for the next coming five years and in the existing year also.

items.statement: Current utilisation at 60-65%, targeting 80-85% by next financial year
items.quote: So after the expansion of our existing capacity, we are running at around 60% to 65% of our existing capacity. So our next year target is that we achieve this to 80% to 85%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will not go below current level
items.quote: Minimum this would be the minimum, I'll never compromise on my EBITDA margin. It would be minimum to the existing level.

items.statement: Adding zinc alloy and aluminium billets for solar to product portfolio
items.quote: We'll be adding zinc alloy, which will require into automobile industries, into electrical equipment manufacturing industries, number two. Number three, your second question was more like it is a capacity game or it is a technology based driven game.

items.statement: Sales prices linked to NALCO, LME, MCX; purchase hedged at percentage of LME
items.quote: Our sales price for deox are linked with NALCO prices and our alloy prices are linked with either with LME or with MCX of aluminium. So we cover ourselves on the sales part also, vice versa on the purchase part also.

items.statement: Personally visit yards globally; use indenting agents; attend BIR and ISRI conferences
items.quote: We personally visit yards. We believe in personal visit in yard in different parts of the world and being the one of the oldest in this industry, we know from where we can get good source of material.

items.statement: Receivables up due to new clientele; short-term borrowings up due to expansion
items.quote: It's mainly due to the expansion, borrowings, short-term borrowings for the expansion as well as receivable is due to the introducing of a new clientele.

items.statement: Company manufactures 3% of India's secondary aluminium alloy
items.quote: Recycling industry, you can say I'm only manufacturing, this Baheti group manufacturers only 3% of secondary aluminium alloy manufacturing, in terms of total manufacturing of secondary aluminium alloy by we stand at 3%.

items.statement: Carbon credit trading not yet active in India; may become relevant in 4-5 years
items.quote: As on date, in India it is not been traded, but in coming next four five years down the line, with the standard of European carbon emissions, even if we have to procure some scrap from Europe or even if we have to sell it locally to the OEMs and die casters, we'll have that carbon emissions per kg.

items.statement: Engaging with die casters in Hungary, Turkey, Germany, UK
items.quote: As you have seen that we have entered into new geography of South Indian market. We have a closely talk with Hungary die casters, which is a very big one die casters and even in Turkey, Germany, U.K.

items.statement: Expansion funding to be decided; internal accruals available
items.quote: That we'll have to decide. We have good internal accruals we can do from that. That we'll decide once the project gets onboard.

items.statement: Aluminium alloy revenue share growing steadily; expect growth for next five years
items.quote: You will see that there is an increment in aluminium alloy revenue percentage, because as I have told you, that in 2018, we have shifted our focus from aluminium ferro alloys to aluminium alloy, and this aluminium alloys, the players, the buyers of aluminium alloy are the big companies, which usually take time to get registered into. That is why, it is on a steady growth, and we expect this growth

items.statement: Order inflows averaging ~3,000 crore per quarter for six consecutive quarters (+/-10%), with backlog near 10,000 crore split 25% large orders and 75% base orders.
items.quote: 3,000 crores, I think, is the sixth coming quarter in a row where we have seen that 6,000 crores has been the ordering flow, roughly, on average. (+/-10%) here and there.

items.statement: Order backlog of ~10,000 crore comprises 25% large orders and 75% base orders; base orders to execute over next four quarters.
items.quote: On the backlog side of it, today we are talking of almost 10,000 crores of orders, which comprises 25 percentage in terms of large orders, and 75 percentage for base orders.

items.statement: Management expects healthy order inflow run rate of 2,500-3,000 crore per quarter; difficult to predict step-up to 4,000 crore but pipeline is strong.
items.quote: So, what we see is that it's a healthy 2,500 to 3,000 crore band for us as the volumes go, and quite frankly, it is very difficult to predict whether when and where it will hit 4,000 crores.

items.statement: PAT margin at 15% driven by revenue mix (exports, services, projects, products) and capacity utilization leverage.
items.quote: On profitability. So, I think we successfully, again, posted a 15% PAT percentage is what we see and that's basically coming from a good mix of revenue between exports, services, projects and products.

items.statement: Cumulative capex of 125 crore in first nine months; ongoing expansions and modernization; annual run-rate 200-250 crore.
items.quote: Cumulative CAPEX is 125 crores is what we see for the last nine months to say and then we still have projects ongoing for the various expansions and modernization of factories and plants.

items.statement: No capacity constraints; adequate headroom in existing plants and land banks for new factories; capacity expansion driven by market demand and productivity improvements.
items.quote: So, to summarize it, we don't see any capacity constraints at this point of time, and we have enough land banks for us in case we have to put up new factories and also the existing factories have the headroom to meet demand surge.

items.statement: Commodity prices and forex stable; pricing dynamic per product/segment; no fixed rule; management decides based on demand-supply.
items.quote: The commodity prices are now stabilized. The forex variation is also now limited because they have also currencies now become stable. So, the pricing is a dynamic stuff. It depends on how the demand and the supply situation behaves in each and every product.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting: products 76%, projects 11-12%, services 12-15%; exports 12% of revenue; EL and Motion 75-80% product business.
items.quote: Next, when it comes to the offerings projects is 11-12%. This is also pretty stable and the products have increased to 76% as a major share.

items.statement: Collections outpacing revenue; inventory building for backlog execution; strong cash position with inventory to liquidate over coming quarters.
items.quote: Cash remains strong. Our collections in the market continued to outpace the revenues as such, but the other part is that we are definitely built upon inventory because we have a backlog to execute.

items.statement: Motion division reached 10 GW milestone in renewable energy automation solutions, up from 5 GW three-four years ago.
items.quote: On the Motion drive product, we have reached a 10-gigawatt milestone in renewable energy automation solution. And only three, four years back, we used to talk about 5-gigawatts.

items.statement: Power distribution market: India 440.85 GW capacity (Apr 2024), projected to double to 817 GW by 2030; ABB portfolio well positioned.
items.quote: India is the third largest producer and consumer of electricity worldwide and with 440.85 gigawatt as of April 30th. So, it is likely to double to 817-gigawatts by 2030.

items.statement: Exports 12% of revenue; exporting to 30+ countries; process automation exports to Middle East and Africa; primarily focused on India and South Asia.
items.quote: In terms of exports, we are 12% of the revenues for the exports, but I think the OEMs and the EPCs and the partners are the same as what it used to be earlier, no major changes what we see.

items.statement: Data center customers (global and local) placing repeat large orders with high value-add; some customers doubling orders within 1.5 months.
items.quote: And in fact, there are positive surprises as well, wherein a customer decided for one project, and they surprised us maybe one-and-a-half months later and said, Hey, I am setting up another one. No questions asked. Please double the supply of number one because I am now setting up two.

items.statement: LT motors facing pricing pressure from competition; ABB maintaining market share through energy efficiency leadership and premiumization.
items.quote: LT motors has been facing some headwinds when it comes to the pricing piece. And of course, large players like ABB who has a substantial market share are affected, I would say, a bit more in advance.

items.statement: Government CAPEX revival in transportation (railways, metros) driving large orders; Make in India campaign deepening local value addition.
items.quote: This is also a reflection of the fact that the government's spend in CAPEX revival especially in transportation segment is helping us and if you see that, it's more to do with the Motion segment as such.

items.statement: Large order execution timing depends on project milestones and customer decisions; design changes (e.g., railway traction) can stretch revenue recognition.
items.quote: So, you have that kind of effect, and you know that design change to get impacted and that's how your large project revenue, even if they were planned for mid-term, they get stretched a little bit, but they definitely come.

items.statement: CSR: Motion team opened electrical machines lab at IIT Mumbai; focus on education, skilling, communities, environment.
items.quote: Recently our Motion team, led by Sanjeev Arora, opened an electrical machines lab in IIT, Mumbai, wherein they have requested to upgrade their machines so that the next generation engineers can really play and train themselves on the best of the machines.

items.statement: FY25 crude oil production target revised to 3.56 MMT; natural gas target maintained at 3.2-3.3 BCM
items.quote: Yes, for the current year, the target, actually, we have created our revised crude oil target. It will be 3.6 million tons, close to 3.6 million tons, yes, 3.56 million tons or something.

items.statement: Long-term vision to achieve 4 MMT oil and 5 BCM gas per year within next couple of years
items.quote: You are aware that the long-term vision of the company in the next few years is to achieve production close to 4 million tons of oil, and 5 BCM of gas per year.

items.quote: So during that period -- during this Q2 period, they had a major shutdown, actually. They didn't operate. And also NRL, what happened is that they had some surplus naphtha during this period. So NRL consumption was also a little bit low

items.quote: I think there will be more upliftment. But on the other hand, there will be a little bit of lower upliftment by the Tea garden, because this is a lean season for the Tea garden. So overall, I think there will be a small increase -- increment.

items.quote: The EBITDA margin for Q2 financial year '25 has decreased by 47.67% vis-a-vis 48.29% for Q2 FY '24, which is mainly due to lower crude oil price.

items.quote: As per the direction of the government that from April '23 onwards, whatever additional activity you do on the new gas that you produce, you will get a premium of 20% over the $6.5 cap that we have.

items.quote: Let's see, the next 3 years, capex projection for the Oil India on internal basis will be in the range of around INR6,000 crores to INR7,000 crores. And on the group basis, if we consider Numaligarh Refinery, it can be around INR10,000 crores to INR12,000 crores.

items.quote: The existing pattern of growth that we have in our commissioned facilities, that's in Uganda and the project pipeline for consultancy as well as the orders in hand for the pharma distribution division, so all those are likely to maintain a robust growth.

items.statement: Europe facing challenges from Chinese car imports and economic struggles in Germany and France

items.statement: Domestic two-wheeler industry showing green shoots in rural demand for 100cc segment

items.statement: Winning significant new contracts globally at the cost of competition

items.statement: Electronics Division gained major ICE OEM as second largest customer, another large ICE OEM coming on board
items.quote: Today one major ICE OEM has become second largest customer to us for the electronics division. And another large OEM ICE manufacturer is becoming a customer.

items.quote: I think within SED there is an internally allocated cases which we don't really disclose the market but which comes within the 180 crore s that we have mentioned in the last quarter

items.statement: SCS restructuring to create single Morocco plant for Europe, lean German ops, Hungarian warehouse, Poland shutdown

items.statement: Freight costs elevated due to Red Sea crisis and container shortage
items.quote: Shortage of containers therefore it has pushed up our freight costs.

items.statement: Matamoros facing 40-50% wage increase over 2 years, restructuring to improve efficiency
items.quote: As I said in 2 years we are something like 40%-50% increase. That cannot be fully offset I think but it will make it a lot more efficient.

items.statement: Domestic Cable Division expanding into braking products beyond cables strategy
items.quote: It is also expanding very well into what we call it as beyond cables strategy, specifically into the braking products.

items.statement: Electronics Division shifting focus from EV to non-EV and ICE OEMs for stable business
items.quote: Now from here our focus has been to move forward and try to get into the non-EV segment and also beyond what we call it as beyond EV is what we are looking at.

items.quote: One of our first big customer for electronics division is no longer buying for us because they're not operating. So, the whole thing has changed.

items.statement: European OEM plant closures create consolidation opportunity for Suprajit's global footprint
items.quote: There will be a lot of consolidation of the industry which you have seen, at least in our industry it has happened. We ourselves have done multiple acquisitions.

items.statement: Matamoros tariff issue in discovery phase with US authorities, resolution expected by March-April
items.quote: The way I look at it by around March-April we should be having some thought of an understanding where we are hopefully.

items.statement: Total debt Rs 717 crore, cash Rs 325 crore as of Sept 30, 2024; debt up 23% QoQ due to India capex and working capital
items.quote: The total debt level was 717 crores as on 30th September 2024. The cash balance was 325 crores as on 30th September 2024 invested in mutual funds and bonds.

items.statement: SCS acquisition Phase 1 spend Rs 94 crore; no change in $13.5M EV but working capital support ongoing
items.quote: There is no change in the EV as such. I don't know exactly the number; it is 13.5 was the EV. But please understand when we took an insolvent company, they didn't have any working capital.

items.statement: SCS China and Canada acquisition expected to close by early January, profitable segment
items.quote: The China part is being done. It will be done sometime hopefully in the early part of January. So, that cost will be there.

items.statement: No further cable asset acquisitions planned; global footprint now complete
items.quote: I don't think we have any plans to do any such cable asset acquisition because I think our footprint is complete in most sense.

items.statement: Target to grow 5-10% above global automotive industry growth (assumed 2-4%) through market share gains

items.statement: SCS EBITDA breakeven expected in 2-3 quarters after China/Canada integration; material cost at 50-55%
items.quote: We see for example the numbers of material cost at 50% to 55% that we know as a cable manufacturer is a good number to b e considering our multi geographical

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 maintained at 11% plus/minus 0.5% at group level
items.quote: we have actually factored all these capex which will come on board. And that's how we are in the guidance of 11% plus minus 0.5% at a group level, and we continue to maintain that guidance.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex including land bank was INR 844 crores; land bank spend ~INR 300 crores in H1
items.quote: The total capex, including the land bank for the first half was at INR 844 crores. While sustaining and growth capex has been financed from business cash flows, the capital expenditure primarily on land bank has resulted in incremental debt.

items.statement: Land-related capex expected ~INR 700 crores total for FY25 (INR 300 crores in H1, ~INR 200 crores prior, ~INR 100-150 crores in H2)
items.quote: the land -related capex, we have spent almost around INR 600 crores to INR 700 crores on land. This first half of INR 300 crores, last time we spent around INR 200-odd crores. And this year, for the rest of the year, we will have maybe around another INR 100 crores to INR 150 crores of investment.

items.statement: EV 2W revenue INR 228 crores in Q2 (up from INR 160 crores QoQ) but profitability still below average due to expansion phase, depreciation on unutilized capacity
items.quote: In terms of profitability, it still is below our average profitability level that we get let the business, gets into a stable phase of us, still into a lot of expansion phase with the capex still being incurred and depreciation, etcetera, which will be awarded on the full capacity, which are not yet ful ly utilized.

items.statement: Wall-mounted charger (EVSE) profitability expected in line with company average at peak capacity
items.quote: So profitably, we are expecting once it reaches the peak capacity, it should be in line with our average profitability.

items.quote: Our associate TRMN inaugurated its new plant at Neemrana, Rajasthan and started commercial production from this plant. i!Ot•)I MINDA] --.:>~ The plant has state-of -the-art manufacturing facility spread over 24 acres. items.statement: Kosei Minda turned profitable; Uno Minda Buehler Motors and EV Systems still below target profitability, ramping up
items.quote: Kosei Minda definitely has come to black, Ashutosh, in terms of profitability. So there's definitely some improvement there. items.statement: Revised FY25 capex guidance upward from INR800 crore to INR1,200 crore
items.quote: On the backdrop of these orders and upcoming opportunities, we are revising our annual CapEx guidance significantly upward from INR800 crores to INR1,200 crores for the year '25.

items.statement: Expect defence product sales of INR1,500 crore with defence reaching around 20% of total sales in FY25
items.quote: We are optimistic of achieving defence product sales of INR1,500 crores, with defence reaching around 20% of our total sales for the year FY '25.

items.statement: Expect to be net debt-free by end of FY25 funded through internal resources and defence order advances
items.quote: And we believe that by the end of this financial year, company should be debt -free with the optimism of defence orders and advances against them.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR5,757 crore with defence at INR3,336 crore and explosives at INR2,224 crore
items.quote: Total order book stands at INR5,757 crores. So out of that, defence stands at around INR3,336 crores and around INR2,224 crores is for explosives.

items.quote: We are happy to highlight that we have recently backed the 2 -year order from Singareni Collieries to the tune of INR887 crores and defence products worth INR1,110 crores, consolidating our current order book to INR5,700 crores plus.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly EBITDA margin at 27.70% and PAT margin at 17.70% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We reported an EBITDA of INR475 crores against INR344 crores showing a decent rise in the margin from 25.52% to 27.70% in the seasonally weak quarter.

items.statement: Expect to sustain 25% plus EBITDA margin going forward but not unreasonably optimistic about 30%
items.quote: And we are reasonably optimistic that we should achieve 25% plus EBITDA margin going forward as well.

items.statement: Domestic demand impacted by elections and heavy monsoon with 8% above normal rainfall impacting mining and infrastructure
items.quote: Our industry has faced subdued demand due to elections and heavy monsoon season, impacting the execution of mining and infrastructure activities in the first half of the year.

items.statement: International business showing positive turnaround in South Africa, Australia and nearby countries after corrective measures
items.quote: We have seen a lot of improvements in South Africa and nearby countries and even in Australia also. So we are expecting and we have seen that those countries are showing a lot of positive turnaround.

items.statement: Defence revenue grew 204% YoY to INR322 crore, now 19% of revenue basket vs 8% last year
items.quote: We are glad to share that the defence section potential has started unfolding with the revenue growth of 204% year -on-year and increasing threefold from INR106 crores to INR322 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: CIL share in customer basket down to 10% from 14%, defence increased to 19% from 8%
items.quote: The percentage of the sectors in the customer basket are as fol lows: CIL is down in the basket to 10% from 14%. Non -CIL & institutional is at 13% from 15%. H&I is at 11% in the basket. items.statement: Capex revised to INR1,200 crore for FY25, expect elevated capex of INR1,000-1,200 crore annually for next 1-2 years
items.quote: Looking at strong opportunities and a lot of orders in pipeline, we believe that there will be enough opportunities where we can invest more than INR1,000 crores or INR1,200 crores on an annualized basis.

items.statement: South Africa, Australia and Southeast Asian subsidiaries now EBITDA positive with licenses and operations started
items.quote: Yes. We have set up the infrastructure. We got the licenses now, and we have started the operations. And now we are EBITDA positive in all those subsidiaries.

items.statement: Raw material prices flat YoY, currently stabilized with 2% fall in realization
items.quote: See, year -on-year basis, the raw material prices have been flat. So as you've see in our realization, it's around 2% fall. So raw material prices have fallen and currently, they have stabilized.

items.quote: So as a result, the inventory, you see the numbers in inventory and the working capital days from 84, it currently stands at 89, which is well within our normal business operations, 90.

items.quote: In this quarter, the international business has delivered INR799 crores revenue, and it includes all those subsidiaries.

items.quote: Our explosive volume for the quarter and half yearly has increased by 7% and 12%, respectively. Initiating Systems revenue increased by 2% in the half year.

items.quote: So 60% to 70% will come from these 2 new sections, and rest 30% will come from our core domestic businesses.

items.quote: Yes. So you know that we have received the order of loitering munitions. So loitering munitions, the drones we have purchased from one of our associates that is Z Motion and then we have supplied that, after adding explosives to it, to the government.

items.quote: You will get the country-wise details at the annual results, which we will share after the end of this financial year.

items.quote: In terms of our order book as of September 30, 2024, we have a net outstanding order book of Rs. 3,610 Crores, which represents almost 3.6x our FY '24 revenues, providing a strong visibility to the investors and to the management.

items.quote: So this year, we expect this segment to do almost Rs. 140 Crores of revenue, which will be a jump from Rs. 95 Crores done last year, which is a significant jump in terms of the Ghana factory, like I said in my opening remarks, the December, we will start the production there and the revenue will start booking in Q4. So 14% to 15% of the pledge is released.

items.statement: Monthly run rate slightly higher than Rs. 100 Crores in Q3 FY25, after achieving ~Rs. 100 Crores in monsoon Q2
items.quote: Yes. We did. We did about Rs. 100 Crores in a monsoon quarter for a construction company, which is the second quarter, we did about Rs. 280 Crores, Rs. 285 Crores, which is almost Rs. 100 Crores kind of run rate

items.statement: Confirmed 45% profit growth guidance for FY25
items.quote: And sir, my last question is for this year, you have guided for a 45% profit growth. So are we like guiding the same for this financial year? Atul Tantia: Yes

items.quote: It's a mix of railways and roads. Today, railway accounts for almost 40% - 45% of our infrastructure order book and balances from NHAI, MoRTH, etc. So it's a mix of both. We are not dominant towards either. The Sleeper business obviously is only railways.

items.statement: Government spending on infrastructure is quite good with continued focus, no expected challenges for order pipeline
items.quote: The government spending on infrastructure is quite good and continued focus on the infrastructure. So we don't expect any challenges with respect to that as well.

items.statement: External credit rating on review by CRISIL, expecting positive movement
items.quote: Our external credit ratin g is also on review by CRISIL, and we expect a positive movement

items.statement: Management targets double-digit EBITDA margin by FY26 through structural cost savings of 4-5% over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: That gives us comfort that structurally we can improve our margin from here by 4% to 5% in 1-1.5 years' timeframe. That will allow us to reach somewhere around (+10%) EBITDA margin level.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin compressed to 4.3% from 8.8% YoY due to input cost inflation
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has compressed to 4.3% this quarter from 8.8% in Q2 last year.

items.statement: Potato prices up 60-65% YoY driving 70-75% of 2% gross margin decline; palm oil duty hike in September adds Q3 pressure
items.quote: Potato prices are higher by about 60% -65% over the previous year and there is some kind of exceptional inflation. We have not seen this kind of inflation, especially in potato earlier.

items.statement: Inflation also seen in wheat, corn, pulses, gram flour; palm oil common across all products
items.quote: unfortunately, this time we are experiencing severe inflation in m ost of the commodities including wheat, corn, pulses, the gram flour etc. So yes, inflation is there even for other commodities as well

items.statement: Mitigating cost inflation via grammage reduction, trade margin rationalization, and PTR increases
items.quote: We are just trying to mitigate most of its negative impact by rationalizing the grammages, by reducing the trade margin, by increasing the price to retailer what we call PTR.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of Rs 20-25 crore including Rs 8-9 crore solar plant; no significant expansion capex planned
items.quote: The overall maintenance CAPEX including some new CAPEX for vehicles and some CAPEX to match the production capacity vis-à-vis packing capacity, the overall CAPEX would be somewhere in the range of say Rs. 20-25 crore.

items.statement: Current utilization ~60%; Jammu and Rajkot plants commissioned last year; Jammu plant now settling and expected to contribute in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: The current utilization level would be Q2 & H1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call Transcript about 60%, so it's only the maintenance CAPEX required and some addition in our fleet because we have our own fleet of about 200 vehicles

items.statement: Large packs (Rs 10+) at 18-20% of revenue; Rs 5 packs >80% of volumes; premium 'Seven Diamond' launched at Rs 30 for quick commerce
items.quote: On an average for the entire company 18% to 20% is the number for large pack, large I mean Rs. 10 and above.

items.statement: Direct distribution model reduced channel cost from 14% to ~10%; some disruption in small distributor markets but largely successful
items.quote: Earlier were following a three-tier distribution model and the overall channel cost, excluding retailer, was about 14%. Now with this direct distribution, the overall distribution cost has come down to about 10%.

items.statement: Exports initiated with shipments dispatched in Q3; participated in SIAL Paris, ISM Dubai, BSM Saudi Arabia with encouraging response
items.quote: initiated exports this quarter and the initial shipments have been dispatched in Q3. Our teams have actively participated in several international trade fairs including SIAL in Paris, ISM in Dubai and BSM in Q2 & H1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call Transcript Saudi Arabia, receiving an encouraging response across all events

items.statement: Industry growth ~5% in western salty; Rs 5 segment under pressure; Prataap gained volume share in Rs 5 packs despite industry stress
items.quote: Industry in the western salty space over the last quarter have been largely in that tune of 5% odd and Rs. 5 should be Neilson numbers are yet to be kind of closely reported.

items.statement: Pellet snacks growing significantly; Rings declining; Potato Chips flat but held share via flavor innovation
items.quote: For us Rings as a product as a category has seen a declining trend on this, Potato Chips have been largely flat. It was being driven by our ability to innovate on the flavours and if you will see we have been able to kind of hold on to our Potato Chips share and numbers despite the core flavours not doing well.

items.statement: J&K incentive income not accrued quarterly; expected to start accruing by March FY25 upon meeting conditions
items.quote: J&K incentive is not yet accrued. As a policy we accrue incentives generally at the end of the financial year, if the benefit is linked to the sales threshold or something like this.

items.statement: Peak XV Partners exited 47% stake in September 2024; acquired by Authum Group and Mahi Madhusudan Kela who initiated open offer
items.quote: In September 2024 our private equity partner Peak XV Partners formerly Sequoia Capital exited their 47% stake in Prataap Snacks achieving a manifold return on investments.

items.quote: So, they just started working in last quarter, so I think it's a bit early. items.statement: Potato fresh crop expected mid-December to ease prices; palm oil volatility makes Q3/FY25 margin guidance difficult

items.statement: SFA implemented across most geographies; DMS rolled back to drawing board after pilot learnings

items.quote: We have had the first listing of our products for our customers one of the quick commerce platforms. items.statement: Manpower cost at 9.5% with 1-1.5% saving potential; overhead savings of ~1% also targeted
items.quote: In our case the overall manpower cost is Q2 & H1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call Transcript about 9.5%, so there is a saving potential about 1%-1.5%, especially in the manpower cost and 1% kind of saving potential we are foreseeing in the rest of the overhead line items

items.statement: Namkeen <20% of revenue but growing; new products and price points to accelerate growth in H2 FY25

items.quote: We closed our 3P operations in Bangalore, integrated the manufacturing lines into our own facility to ensure seamless service to key markets while reducing overhead costs. items.quote: we are trying to put discounts and liquidate the stocks, but you should also find out from the peers there is also a, what do you call that, there is a leeway from the government, where like whatever non -BIS stock is already in the distribution channels or like the other channels like retail channels, they will not come and hold us liable for that.

items.quote: So Q3, we are targeting that we should close somewhere around INR370 crores to INR400 crores. And in Q4 -- the balance would be Q4.

items.quote: So we don't -- nearly need to do any kind of a capex to increase our production capacity. It can be increased by adding more and more job workers which are readily available in the market.

items.quote: We are pleased to share that project Lakshya's share of domestic sales rose from 26% in FY '24 to 31% in H1 FY '25.

items.statement: Strong thermal demand expected in Q3 due to longer winter forecast

items.statement: Force NXT grew 30% value and 38% volume YoY in Q2; premium mix driving ASP improvement
items.quote: Force NXT accounted for about 5% of our revenue in quarter 2 FY '25, showing a 30% growth in the value and a 38% increase in volume terms Y-o-Y.

items.statement: No price hikes taken in FY24 or FY25; ASP increase driven by product mix shift to premium

items.statement: Targets working capital days of 135-140 by FY26; aims to be debt-free by FY27/28
items.quote: our target is to reduce working capital days by FY '26, around 135 to 140 days. And we have the internal target to become debt-free. Srinath Sridhar: By when? Ajay Patodia: By FY '27/'28

items.quote: So it's cyclical. Vijay Ji, it's cyclical because during this period, we restock up the thermal goods also, which is higher ASP products and higher cost products as well, which will get sold off in quarter 3.

items.statement: Advertising spend of INR56 crores in H1 FY25; targets INR100 crores for full year
items.quote: This year till half yearly -- on a half yearly basis, we have spent around INR31 crores, which is equal to the amount that we spent last year -- sorry, INR56 crores, which was around INR58 crores in last year's 6 months. items.statement: Bangladesh unrest will not impact hosiery industry as minimal manufacturing there

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 13-15% for FY25 driven by high single-digit patient volume growth

items.quote: we are continuing to, like we said, target to 13% to 15% revenue growth and margins at about between 26% to 27%

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisition targets in advanced specialty testing and North India expansion; advanced stages of evaluation

items.statement: Goal to double combined business organically over next five years with M&A as accelerator

items.statement: BIOSECURE Act driving supply chain diversification discussions and early traction

items.quote: Of two pending Phase-3 readouts, glad to inform you that one yielded a positive result.

items.statement: Suven spent Rs694 million capex in H1 FY25 on R&D center Phase-1 and Suryapet plant
items.quote: A total of Rs.694 million on CAPEX, primarily on Phase-1 of our R&D center at Genome Valley of which 229 has been operational since June '24 and on the Suryapet plant of approximately Rs.164 million.

items.statement: Investing in Phase-1 GMP facility at US-FDA approved plant to accelerate Oligonucleotide customer onboarding
items.quote: With an investment in Phase-1 of its GMP facility which is underway in one of the US -FDA regulatory approved plant s which will accelerate the customer onboarding as well and the commercialization of the projects

items.statement: Cohance H1 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 25.4%; Q2 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 30.3%

items.statement: RFQs sustaining healthy mix of mid-phase, lateral and commercial projects; broader customer base
items.quote: RFQs continue to sustain a healthy mix of mid-phase and lateral project which is one of the strategic intent that we have taken including some of the commercials as well. RFQs now are coming in from a broader set of customers versus history.

items.statement: Augmented business development team across US, Europe, Asia to deepen engagement with large innovators and biotech firms

items.statement: Added lateral commercial products with case studies in recent quarters

items.statement: Positive sentiment towards India CDMO bolstered by supply chain diversification and BIOSECURE Act
items.quote: Positive sentiment towards India is bolstered by efforts to diversify and stabilize supply chain and supportive macro environment trends including the US BIOSECURE Act.

items.statement: Merger with Cohance received Stock Exchange and SEBI approval; NCLT shareholder meeting scheduled 28 Nov 2024
items.quote: Regarding the proposed merger with Cohance, we have received approval from Stock Exchange in Sebi, and we have received an order from the Honorable NCLT Mumbai Bench to host the shareholder meeting for the voting on the merger. The meeting is scheduled for 28th November 2024.

items.statement: Expect merger completion in 4-6 months subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals
items.quote: Subject to shareholder and other regulatory approvals, we expect the merger to complete in next 4 to 6 months.

items.statement: Suven generated Rs1.10 billion free cash flow in H1 FY25; cash balance Rs6.56 billion at Sep 2024
items.quote: In the first half, Suven has generated a free cash flow of Rs. 1.10 billion with the cash and bank balance standing at 6.56 billion at the end of September '24.

items.statement: Strategy includes inorganic acquisitions to add capabilities; will continue evaluating opportunities
items.quote: We will continue to look at capabilities that are better to buy than built. So, that is a key part of our strategy and we will continue to evaluate those opportunities as they come across.

items.quote: Chinese and Indonesian subsidiaries have performed satisfactorily.

items.quote: On the EBITDA per TEU, so rail is at about INR9,800. CFS, if you look at the pure operational one, it's about INR1,200 - INR1,300, there were some recurring one-offs over there.

items.quote: In terms of overall volume, Q2 was much better than Q1 like we've seen in the overall numbers. items.statement: Faridabad terminal now double-stack operational (10 days ago), improving turnaround and decongesting Garhi Harsaru
items.quote: In terms of infrastructure, now the latest thing for us is that Faridabad is double stack. This has happened about 10 days ago. So now we're running direct double-stack services rather than pumping it at other locations, which improves our turnaround time, service levels to the customer and a slight reduction in cost.

items.statement: Hopes to maintain Q2 rail volumes for rest of FY25; H2 FY25 expected higher than H2 FY24 but full-year YoY uncertain
items.quote: So volume is still hard to say going forward, what it will be like. But hopefully, we can just keep up the Q2 kind of numbers for the rest of t he year. It's still subdued overall in terms of the Red Sea crisis is continuing.

items.statement: Jaipur ICD delayed due to land parcel unavailability; actively negotiating for one new location; no expansion plans on hold
items.quote: As far as Jaipur is concerned, there are a couple of parcels of land which are not available to us as reported earlier and we're trying to get some additional land. But again, the contiguity and difficulty in getting some additional land and the price at which it is avail able now, it is making it unviable.

items.statement: CFS margins under pressure due to R&M at 25-year-old Bombay facility, arbitration costs, labor cost increases, and competitive pricing
items.quote: CFS margins are under pressure. Revenue wise, it's not that big of a difference. From the EBITDA level, there is a drop because Bombay also especially is a 25-year-old facility. We are revamping it. So there's a lot of R&M going towards that.

items.statement: CFS revenue per TEU below INR7,000 due to ground rent decline, H&T rate slip, and INR20 cr accounting change to net revenue recognition
items.quote: Yes. Basically the 30 - 35 CFS is through and DPD is also increasing. Ground rent is actually going down. That is a general trend that's been happening for the last few years and H&T rates are also slipping a little bit.

items.quote: So we are not seeing a major problem as far as the imbalance is concerned because it is still in the ratio of like 55%, 45%. 55% is the import side and 45% is the export side.

items.statement: Kashipur volumes have scope to increase; key customers won, impact expected from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Kashipur volumes have a lot of scope to increase. There are some key customers that we won and we'll probably see that impact coming in Q4.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis continuing; low-value commodity cargo not back to prior levels; macros subdued

So, we acquired that lab and merged that into Smileworks and started Smileworks with all the expertise which Dr. Ankur Gupta and Mr. Lalit Sharma had with that lab. So, they are now 40% partners in the lab and 60% is with Vasa.

items.quote: Our margins declined in the H1, as typically H1 faces delays in project logistics and ODC, which has high margins due to heavy rains, limited infrastructure project approvals, and this year, delays were also caused by election as well.

items.quote: project logistics and over-dimensional cargo, they have 12% plus margin at all times and talking about general logistics and contracted integrated logistics, there are about 12 and below 12 at all times.

items.quote: we do see around Rs. 10 crores of capital expenditure happening in this particular half, which could further boost our sales and also give us an opportunity to cater to demands and needs which we would have not done earlier.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: 47% general logistics, 29% contracted integrated, 21% project, 3% ODC; H2 expected >60% project+ODC

items.statement: Added high-quality marquee clients post-IPO; targeting top-tier customers with ESG requirements; secured EV vehicle trial order from a top client
items.quote: we are able to get the best of the best clients in this industry and they are respecting us. They are giving us an opportunity to meet and they are giving us an opportunity to execute large projects as well.

items.statement: Targeting debtor days reduction from current ~110 days to 100 days; two large infrastructure clients' payments stuck due to Maldives geopolitical issues
items.quote: we are definitely working very, very hard to get that number down of debtor days. And we are focusing on quality clients, and we are focusing on clients where the number of debtors days can be reduced to say, a hundred days maximum.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity reduced to 0.05x; H2 borrowings may increase if order demand requires, finance cost uncertain
items.quote: The debt to equity at the ratio came down to 0.05x.

items.statement: Acquired PRL Supply Chain Solutions as wholly owned subsidiary for international freight forwarding, warehousing, and project logistics
items.quote: We also had a notable acquisition which is PRL Supply Chain Solutions as a wholly owned subsidiary. So, this will enhance our service offerings in supply chain management across international markets as well now.

items.statement: H1 FY25: 15,735 orders, 594 customers, average revenue per order Rs 71,599; ROE 18%, ROCE 19%
items.quote: On the operational front, we did 15,735 orders and served 594 customers with an average revenue per order at 71,599.

items.statement: Receivables concentration risk: two large clients' payments delayed due to Maldives geopolitical distress; no legal action initiated to preserve relationship
items.quote: these are two big companies which are existing in India. items.quote: As mentioned at our last call, with some tailwinds and changes in the market conditions, we anticipate that the second half of the fiscal to be better overall.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% more SIOP volumes in H2 vs H1 with stable margins
items.quote: We anticipate that we would do around 20% to 25% more volumes in H2 compared to H1. And we anticipate the margins to be stable.

items.statement: Renewable energy project expected to be operational by Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our renewable energy project is also on the verge of completion and is expected to be up and running by quarter 4 of this year.

items.statement: C-PVC capacity currently 20,000 tons at 100% utilization; expanding to 50,000 tons
items.quote: So current capacity for C-PVC is around 20,000 tons, and after the doubling of the capacity, we are utilizing 100%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 utilization: soda ash 88%, caustic soda 78%, PVC ~100%, SIOP 88%, C-PVC 100%
items.quote: The utilization levels for the quarter were as follows: 88% for soda ash, 78% for caustic soda and PVC around 100%. SIOP improved to 88% and C-PVC at 100%.

items.statement: PVC industry demand strong with growth in domestic consumption vs last fiscal
items.quote: The PVC industry remains strong on the demand front, and we are seeing a growth in overall domestic consumption compared to the last fiscal.

items.statement: Synthetic rutile export demand pickup slower than anticipated; stability expected from Q4
items.quote: Going forward, we see some stability coming in our synthetic rutile exports from quarter 4. However, the pickup in demand is slower than anticipated.

items.quote: On the segmental basis, the company recorded an EBITDA of INR48 crores in specialty segment for the said quarter, a surge of 50% Y-o-Y on back of commercialization of recently concluded capex.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBITDA INR35 crore, down 15% YoY; margin 7.2%; net loss INR1.2 crore

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA INR81 crore, down 13% YoY; margin 8.2%; net profit INR5.5 crore, down 57% YoY

items.quote: For DCW, the commodity segment continues to see significant pressure on pricing across the products with net realizations correcting between 3% to 9%, except for synthetic rutile, which has corrected by 27% due to sluggish export demand.

items.quote: We have our own power plant to generate the power required for caustic soda. It's a coal-based plant as of now, and the power cost is in the range of INR7.5 to INR8 per unit.

items.quote: Antidumping duty on C-PVC has been notified by the Finance Ministry in quarter 2 for a period of 5 years, and this will provide pricing stability to the domestic manufacturers.

items.statement: C-PVC import quantity in India currently north of 200,000 tons

items.quote: So, standalone basis, I would say we would still b e close to between Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 5,200 crores. So, yes, we still maintain that there would be a growth of 8% to 10

items.quote: we are on a very good track not only to exceed our Rs.500 Crores, but we will probably be quite close to Rs.1,000 Crores invested in India in the very few years to come when all our investment program me and ideas will materialize

items.statement: Vesuvius India has already invested close to Rs 360 crore in the last 2.5 years; further capex is in pipeline at various approval stages.
items.quote: If you look at Vesuvius India Limited, if you just look at last 2.5 half years numbers which are in public domain, you will see that we have already invested close to Rs.360 Crores that is available in public domain.

items.statement: Rs 1,000 crore group-level investment in India will occur over the next 3-5 years.
items.quote: This Rs.1000 Crores investment in India will happen over the next three to five years.

items.statement: Two new production lines (AlSi Monolithic and Basic Monolithic) totalling 250,000 tonnes inaugurated at Vizag; capacity immediately available.
items.quote: the 250,000 ton nes are basically here today because we inaugurated them today. So, in fact, it is the end of the year, between the end of November and beginning of December, but these 250,000 tonnes will hit the ground in the coming few weeks

items.statement: Kolkata VISO plant capacity increased 50% recently; further expansion planned with land available.
items.quote: We have achieved a few months ago a capacity increase of 50%. We are already studying the next step of further increase of our capacity in Kolkata. And yes, we have the room available to do it.

items.statement: New plastics plant to come on stream next year; additional product lines planned for Vizag.
items.quote: We will have a new plastics plant which will come on stream next year. And we have already on the drawing board many other ideas which will be discussed when implementation will be launched.

items.statement: Steel consumption in India is doing quite well; long-term fundamentals unchanged despite short-term import pressure and low steel prices.
items.quote: If you look at steel consumption, it is doing quite well in India. What you call a slowdown is more associated to an increase in imports in India and to a decline or a low point of steel pri ces which are mostly associated with the fact that the Chinese have been increasing very significantly their export to the rest of the

items.statement: India is the fastest growing steel market; 90% of global steel growth is in India via blast furnaces.
items.quote: fastest growing steel country in the world everything is blast furnace. So today if you look at the world, everybody talks about decarbonization, but all the growth, 90% of the growth in the steel industry, which is today happening in India, is happening with good old blast furnaces and coking coal

items.statement: No forward margin guidance; focus on high-tech products and cost discipline to sustain margins.
items.quote: We do not give forward guidance on the margin evolution of the company. However, I would like to say, we constantly strive to sustain the margin levels that we are and probably the biggest lever that we have to sustain, there are actually two levers that we have to sustain our margin position.

items.statement: Margin expansion only possible by sharing value created through innovation with customers.
items.quote: We can only improve margin if our customers improve also their margin wit h our products. We cannot improve our margin at the expense of customers. It never works. We can only expand margin if we help our customers improve their own margin

items.statement: Alumina and magnesia raw material prices rising; Vesuvius will pass on cost increases to customers.
items.quote: Alumina price is expected to continue to g row stronger which is coming from number of external market factors especially from a capacity of alumina production out of Australia as well as some bauxite supply out of Guyana

items.statement: Refractory companies cannot sell at a loss; alumina-based product prices will be increased regardless of steel prices.
items.quote: We will increase the prices of alumina based product whatever and we will explain as we have done for the past 50 years to our steel customers that we are really sorry and it is not a lack of solidarity.

items.statement: New product sales (products not existing 5 years ago) now 18% of sales, targeting above 20% from next year; flow control higher.
items.quote: New product sales is very simple. It is the percentage of sales in a given year made with product, which did not exist five years before. And this percentage, which used to be a little bit less than 10%, between 9% and 10% eight years ago, is now 18%. And we believe that we will reach and stabilize at above 20% as from next year.

items.statement: Mold flux plant commissioned at Vizag; producing same quality as German plant; targeting market share growth.
items.quote: We are already, since a few weeks now producing in India the same quality products as the one we have been historically producing in our metallurgical plant in Germany. And again, same reasoning as for the other product line, we are very much aware that competitors are also increasing capacity in India in the same product lines so be it.

items.statement: Partnership model with most major steel customers; share value creation via performance contracts.
items.quote: When we work together with a partnership, it is not just you take the benefits. We are also working well with the customer, and they are also seeing benefits that are passed on to them. And this is something which is unique and we have been practicing this and we are working very well.

items.statement: Growing presence in mini-mills as they upgrade to higher-value alloys; induction furnace segment under study.
items.quote: We are seeing very good momentum and very positive progress in what we call mini mills and we start to see engagement in these plants not only on core structure but more so on quality and performance.

items.statement: Welcome competition; it drives innovation. Vesuvius holds 50-55% share in its niche areas globally.
items.quote: We welcome competition. I think competition is what keeps us on our toes, is what forces us to be even better in innovating. So not only we do not fear competition, but we really welcome competition.

items.statement: India capacity primarily for domestic market; opportunistic exports to Southeast Asia continue.
items.quote: our business model is not to export. W e do not use today and we have no plan to use in the future India as a base mostly for export. It does not mean that we will not export from India. We are already exporting a little bit of our production from India to Southeast Asia in

items.statement: TRMS (Total Refractory Management Services) share of sales may increase slightly in India due to customer preference.
items.quote: I tend to say yes. I t end to say yes, that it will. I think that will be a fair assumption

items.statement: Patrick André expects Vesuvius India to at least double turnover over the coming 5-10 years.
items.quote: I would be very disappointed in the coming few years, I do not know if it is five years or six years or four years, but if in the coming 5 to 10 years, Vesuvius will not at least double its turnover, I would be very disappointed.

items.statement: People are the cornerstone; dignity, integrity and trust drive performance.
items.quote: Vesuvius is all about people, not just in India, all over the world. It is all about people. And as I was telling in the afternoon that people are our cornerstones. This is something that we continuously believe.

items.statement: Steel industry is cyclical; difficult years inevitable but long-term India outlook remains very positive.
items.quote: We will have difficult years. I do not know if it is now or if it is 5 years from now or 10 years from now, but it is impossible in the steel market to have only good years after good years. I have never seen that in 35 years.

items.statement: Decarbonization shift to hydrogen has little impact on flow control; advanced refractory demand may even increase.
items.quote: The global answer is in fact, it has very little impact on us. For several reasons, first because our flow control products, which are the main foundation of the Vesuvius business, are consumed as you know at the continuous casting stage of the steel process.

items.statement: No acquisitions planned just because of cash; investments only when they make business sense.
items.quote: We do not want to do acquisitions because we are sitting on cash. We do not want to increase our capacity because we are sitting on cash. We would like to invest it when it makes business sense and that is the plan going forward as well.

items.statement: Fair relationship with customers allows pass-through of raw material cost increases.
items.quote: Typically, we come to the term where we are able to have a fair argument around the cost increase and compensation for it.

items.statement: Management reiterated full-year PAT growth guidance of 20% YoY for FY25
items.quote: We will stick to the same guidance. That's about it.

items.statement: Management indicated Q3 FY25 revenue will be weaker than Q2 FY25 but full-year PAT growth guidance of 20% maintained
items.quote: I think December quarter will be weaker than Q2, that much I can tell you and we have some tail that is left. That's the best I can answer. And I think the new guidance we have given that we'll do 20% better than last year.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain current operating margins of ~60% for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: No, it will maintain the same margin that we have, I think with this year and next year.

items.statement: Revlimid market share reached ~1/3 in Q2 FY25; no challenges expected for remainder of FY25
items.quote: I think we've done all right. at least for this financial year, we don't expect any challenges.

items.statement: Post-Revlimid pipeline includes Semaglutide (diabetes settled, weight-loss in litigation), Olaparib (filed, awaiting approval, 50-50 with Alembic), Erdafitinib, Capmatinib, Carfilzomib 10mg, Bosentan 32mg
items.quote: The biggest one is Semaglutide. So, there are two formulations of Semaglutide, of which one formulation we have is already there in the public domain, and the second one is not settled yet. And the one that is settled, I think two strengths we have sole FTF and other strengths we have shared FTF. The one that is not settled, we are sole FTF, so that's still under litigation. items.statement: Tabrecta added as sole FTF (~$110-120M market); Kyprolis and Jevtana added to shared FTF pipeline
items.quote: I think product is about INR110 million, INR120 million. I don't collect the exact sale. And it is sole FTF, and this is going to be marketed by our entity in the U.S. So we get to keep 100% economics.

items.statement: R&D spend in Q2 FY25 was INR100-125 crores on bio-studies and exhibit batches
items.quote: For example, this quarter, we spent just on R&D, bio-studies and exhibit batches, we spent almost INR100 crores, INR125 crores.

items.statement: Cash balance of ~INR2,600 crores as of end-September 2024; expected to increase by year-end
items.quote: As of end of September, I think we have about INR2,600 crores of cash. And let's see how things go, yes. So I think it will only increase as the year-end.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions in RoW markets; transaction sizes range from $3M to $5-6M; open to larger deals using cash and potential debt/equity
items.quote: We're looking at one transaction, which is about $3 million transaction, we are looking at one transaction which is about $5 million, $6 million. So I mean, you get different types of transactions. But what you consummate in the end it all depends on if we're able to take you on the price and the diligence goes well.

items.statement: Board declared second interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share for FY25
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared a second interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share for FY '24, '25.

items.statement: Domestic pharma business stable but flat; expects 15-20% CAGR over 2-3 years driven by Semaglutide and other launches
items.quote: I think my expectation is that Semaglutide should really jump start this business. That's probably the biggest launch we have. But we also have some smaller launches. So, if you take a 2- to 3-year perspective, I think the business should do well. We expect the business to compound at 15%, 20%.

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences (agro) business losing ~INR40-50 crores annually; target break-even by March 2026, profitability by March 2027
items.quote: I think we're losing about INR40 crores, INR50 crores a year. I think the objective first is that by '26 March, we want to break even. I think that is the internal objective that we have given in the group. So we expect that it will break even I think. So to answer your question, yes, I think '26 March is our target that we should break even in that business.

items.statement: Semaglutide strategy: biggest opportunity in US and India; Mylan has regulated market rights; expanding in Middle East (Saudi), Philippines, Indonesia, China via partners
items.quote: I think the biggest opportunity we see for this product right now is in India and U.S. and Mylan has the rights for the regulated market. So, they'll open up and they actually opened up, I'm seeing some RoW opportunity, but not as much as like what other people are projecting.

items.statement: Management acknowledges high volatility in earnings due to reliance on disruptive products; base portfolio erodes 30-40% every 5 years; no growth without new pipeline
items.quote: If you just look at your own balance sheet, I mean, I can challenge you on any balance sheet. If you look at your own core portfolio, whatever you have on your base goes away 30%, 40% of it goes away in 5 years. So just if you ask me, I don't think it's the correct question. I think you need to judge a person on the pipeline, not on the base. Base means nothing. Base erode continuously, especially

items.statement: Multiple Indian players (Dr. Reddy's, Sun Pharma, NATCO) filed Semaglutide in India; expect most to launch in first wave post-2026 patent expiry
items.quote: Nobody got approval, my friend. Everybody has filed it in India. I mean, Reddy's has filed, I know Sun has filed, we have filed. These are some companies I named. I'm not naming everyone. So, we should assume that most these guys will turn up on the first phase.

items.statement: US generic pricing environment stable for differentiated portfolio; profitability driven by first-wave generics and pipeline depth
items.quote: Overall, the business, I think you have a good portfolio and breath of portfolio, you do reasonably well. I think that's one. The second thing is you need to have good pipelines, which are first wave generics, which gives you a good amount of profitability.

items.statement: FY26 new order inflow target of INR5,000-6,000 crores, maintaining 50-50 private-government mix
items.quote: And going forward, in the next financial year, maybe anywhere between INR5,000 crores to INR6,000 crores new orders.

items.quote: Currently, the bid pipeline as it stands, is about INR5,000 crore.

items.quote: Bihar working capital has actually improved. All our dues have been certified, and we should see them being cleared in this financial year, rest of the financial year. Bengal, we are not executing any government jobs as we speak. So -- and all the earlier jobs have been finished.

items.quote: We aim to get it down to anywhere between 7% to 7.5%. That is what our internal -- our planning is. But as I mentioned earlier, and you also sort of alluded to that, it all depends on our revenue, on our a ctual execution on the ground

items.statement: NGT/GRAP-IV restrictions in NCR (30% of order book) to impact Q3 FY25 execution and margins; labour shortage structural until government upskilling/NREGA reforms
items.quote: one factor which will continue to impact us in this quarter, the ongoing quarter is the NGT, right? So all of you are aware of what's happening in NCR. So now GRAP -IV is in place and -- so that is another thing, which is going to impact this quarter. That's why I've kept the margin guidance muted for the rest of the year, because we have a lot of large p rojects in NCR, especially Gurgaon

items.quote: Labour shortage, the kind of labour shortage that we are seeing now, I mentioned in my last 2 calls that this is virtually an epidemic, which is waiting to be upon us. So labour shortage until the government steps in, I don't think anything much is going to happen. So tha

items.quote: So to specifically answer your question, as far as this financial year is concerned, we are looking at a turnover of about -- we're targeting a turnover of about INR300 crores. And as far as the next financial year is concerned, as Vikas just said, INR70 crores to INR80 crores per month would be an average. That's about INR800 crores give or take a few crores here and there for the next financial

items.statement: Jewellery Park project NTP expected December, design phase then, revenue from H2 FY26 at INR30-50 cr/month initially
