So that is what is going to happen in this case. I mean very honestly. Maybe next year, again, an average run rate of about INR30 crores to INR50 crores in the first few months.

items.statement: Mobilization advance INR542 cr, unbilled revenue INR598 cr, retention money INR335 cr as of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Yes, mobilization advance is 542 and unbilled revenue is 598 and retention is 335.

items.statement: Management targets 50% year-on-year growth for FY26 and aims to improve EBITDA margin by 2-3 percentage points to 13-14%
items.quote: Yes, we do absolutely we do want to do that. We want to get numbers, we want to get those EBITDA and we want to get those PATs definitely, and we are working really hard towards it.

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected to deliver 50% year-on-year growth
items.quote: H2 FY25 as we have already stated, that we are seeing the growth on overall basis of 50% growth on a year-to-year basis, so which we may think we may achieve.

items.statement: Current order book stands at over 350 crores with pipeline of quoted tenders worth nearly 300 crores
items.quote: Current order book is +350 crore and in pipeline we have almost quoted tenders worth about another close to 300 odd crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for Q2 FY25 was 10.3% and H1 FY25 was 11.86%; management aims to raise margin by 2-3% to 13-14% in FY26
items.quote: We definitely want to do that.

items.statement: Acquired controlling stake in Peter Electrical Company Limited to expand manufacturing of electrical panels, compact substations and bus cutting systems
items.quote: We have taken a controlling stake in Peter Electrical Company Limited allowing us to expand our manufacturing capabilities for electrical panels, compact substation and bus cutting system.

items.statement: Government initiatives like RDSS, Saubhagya and PM-Surya Ghar create substantial opportunities; Rajasthan alone launched ~25,000 crores of electrical works
items.quote: Rajasthan just launched about almost about 25,000 crores of electrical works very recently, they published about 25,000 crores of work.

items.statement: Power Minister indicated 30-35 lakh crores outlay for power infrastructure over next five years (~8-10 lakh crores annually)
items.quote: the outlay of funds that they are talking about is almost close to in next five years they are all talking about, deploying about 30 to 35 lakh crores for the power infra.

items.statement: Exploring solar EPC and battery energy storage systems (BESS) as turnkey EPC contractor; targeting innovative products by FY25-26
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are exploring new avenues in solar EPC and battery energy solar systems as a part of our renewable energy initiative, with an increasing focus on R&D, we aim to introduce innovative products by FY25-26.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 120 to 78 days (Mar 2024) and 152 to 100 days; receivables focus to manage cash flow
items.quote: for the same 31st March 2024 we had an inventory days of 120 days, which has been reduced to 78 days. And inventory days of 152 days, which has been reduced 100 days.

items.statement: Reducing finance cost by parking idle money in interest-bearing accounts, optimizing bank guarantee charges and negotiating lower rates with bankers
items.quote: we are effectively utilizing the money like ideal money has been parked to the interest bearing account so that necessary steps are taken to reduce the finance cost in terms of interest, like bank guarantee issuance charges, and we are continuously in touch with bankers to get the rates even reduced.

items.statement: Secured 28.41 crore contract under Mukhya Mantri Ujjwal Jharkhand Yojana; appointed by AAI for Udaipur airport power supply; contract with Adani Group for Ahmedabad airport
items.quote: we have successfully secured a substantial contract under the Mukhya Mantri Ujjwal Jharkhand Yojana, amounting to about 28.41 crores.

items.statement: Geographic footprint covers nearly all states; recently expanded to Himachal, resumed Jharkhand, active in Assam, Rajasthan, Delhi, Manipur, Kerala
items.quote: we have explored our, we have put our foot in Himachal and Jharkhand we have again, we earlier worked in Jharkhand, we opened our account in Jharkhand.

items.statement: Evolving regulatory framework is supportive and acts as a booster; no negative impact foreseen
items.quote: the latest whatever notifications which have come out, on whatever regulations, the upgradation which has been done is very, very supportive. It's very, very supportive in fact it is going to boost the business and there's nothing negative about it.

items.statement: No major operational challenges; projects running smoothly with government support; only seasonal weather impacts
items.quote: We are not facing any challenges, the work are going on smooth, absolutely, there is no issue, the government is very supportive, the government wants the work should be finished on time.

items.statement: Open to international expansion if opportunity, timing and profits are right
items.quote: If given an opportunity, why not, definitely why not, why restrict yourself to just being a domestic player, you can as well be a global player.

items.statement: Focusing on margin improvement over volume; quoting at higher rates to protect EBITDA and PAT rather than chasing top-line growth
items.quote: Right now I am sitting on a good order book. So, I love to now focus on my EBITDA and my PAT instead of just on my top line.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target Rs.675 crore, EBITDA margin 21-23%, PAT margin 12-14%
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, I had projected a combined revenue of Rs.675 crore as against Rs.522 crores, which we had achieved last year , this is close to I would say, 30% growth .

items.statement: Rodney Hunt FY25 revenue target USD 33-36 million vs USD 24.6 million last year
items.quote: We are now looking at revenue anywhere between USD 33 million to as high as USD 36 million in comparison to last year we did $24.6.

items.statement: FY26 capacity expansion to Rs.1000 crore revenue capability with two new plants
items.quote: these two plants coming online in FY26 we would be in a position to ensure that by FY28 we can double our revenue to Rs.1000 crore

items.statement: Order book Rs.873 crore as of 1st November, down from Rs.950 crore due to October dispatches
items.quote: Our order book position is quite strong. It stands at Rs.873 crore as of 1st November. So, we had significant dispatches taking place in October, and that is why the combined order position has come down in the month of November.

items.statement: Expect FY25 year-end order book Rs.850-1000 crore after Rs.450-500 crore new orders in Q3-Q4
items.quote: In the next four months, we expect to achieve additional order book of Rs.450- 500 crore. To close the year, between Rs.850-1000 crore.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 21-23% for FY25, up from ~19-20% last year
items.quote: I informed that we will be at the end of the year, it would be between 21-23%. If you see our EBITDA last year was also on consolidated basis close to 19% .

items.statement: Rodney Hunt PAT margin was 8-9% last year, targeting improvement this year
items.quote: last year Jash Engineering Limited we did around 8-9% PAT and we have already achieved 8-9% last year, and this year, we hope to improve on it

items.statement: Two new plants at Chennai and SEZ Pithampur commissioning in FY26

items.statement: Plan new US plant in 2026-2027 to meet 95% BABA Act requirement after 2029
items.quote: We are expanding in America also in 2026 and in 2027 we aim to put up a new plant in America to address requi rement after 2029

items.statement: No slowdown in bid pipeline, order inflow chart consistently trending upward

But if you see chart of our order inflow you will observe that it is always on the upside, it is going up and up.

items.statement: Refocusing on Middle East and Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Vietnam, Cambodia) for growth
items.quote: We are refocusing our efforts in Middle East, so as to grow faster in that market. As well as we are now trying to enter new markets. We have been quite successful in Vietnam, and now we are expecting business in Cambodia also.

items.statement: Water control gates 59% of revenue, screening 22%, valves 10%, process/pumping 9%
items.quote: As I said before, water control gates is our main business and main product. It contributes 59% over revenue. Thereafter we come screening equipment which contributes close to 22% over revenue, then the valves, including the bulk solid valves, as well as knife gate valves and whatever control valves which contribute 10% to our revenue. items.statement: ~60% revenue from exports, spread across Europe, USA, Middle East, Far East, India
items.quote: This company is primarily now an export based company with more business coming from outside India. Presently, we do close to 60% of revenue outside India. And we are fairly spread everywhere in the world.

items.statement: Top-tier IBM partner, nearing top-tier Cisco partnership, selective investment in vendor certifications
items.quote: If you look at currently, we are in the topmost ti er of partnership with IBM. Cisco, I think we are in the verge of becoming the top tier very soon . Our team is working on it

items.statement: Management targets 15-20% annual revenue growth and aims to reach double-digit EBITDA margin in 3-5 years.
items.quote: It's difficult to predi ct, but yes, we will be easily growing anywhere between 15% to 20% annually. And we will also focus on margin expansions while we grow our topline

items.statement: Management aims for EBOs to contribute ~50% of revenue within 5 years.
items.quote: our aim is to reach about 50% of our topl ine coming out of EBOs over the next 5 years

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 16.48 crore allocated for CAPEX to open 65 COCO and 25 COFO EBOs over 2-3 years.
items.quote: we are planning to open 65 more EBOs over next 2-3 years and 25 more o n FOFO model. So, total Rs. 16.48 crores is what we will be using as CAPEX for EBOs

items.statement: No manufacturing CAPEX planned for the next 1-2 years as outsourcing ratio increases.
items.quote: In terms of any CAPEX for manufacturing, we don't have any plans for next one or two years.

items.statement: IPO of 49.6 lakh shares at Rs 131 each raised Rs 64.976 crore for EBO CAPEX, working capital, and general corporate expenses.
items.quote: We have completed our IPO of 49,60,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each at an issue price of Rs. 131 per equity share amounting to Rs. 64.976 Crore.

items.statement: EBO footprint 16,000 sq ft across 34 stores (avg 472 sq ft); annualized sales per sq ft Rs 16,048.
items.quote: Our EBO footprint spans 16,000 square feet, with an average store size of 472 square feet. The average sales price is ₹1,600. and the average bill ing value is ₹3,620, while our annualized sales per square foot stand at ₹16,048

items.statement: Same-store sales growth for COCO+COFO EBOs is double-digit in H1 FY25.
items.quote: we are tracking this same store sales growth f or our internal purposes and it's a double digit growth as we speak for the first half year

items.statement: Revenue mix H1 FY25: offline trade 55%, EBO 13%, LFS 8%, online 18%, exports/direct 6%.
items.quote: For H1, 55% of revenue came from offline trade, 13% from EBOs, 8% from Large format stores, and 18% from our online business and balance 6% from exports and direct sales.

items.statement: North and West India account for ~80% of revenue; expansion focus remains on these regions.
items.quote: Our presence is concentra ted in northern and western India, which collectively accounts approximately 80% of our revenue due to robust demand, and we aim to focus on these regions for further expansion

items.statement: Pricing lever underutilized; room to increase prices as EBO/e-com channels grow; no need to cut prices.
items.quote: we are in fact using the lever and using it to our advanta ge. So, we expect the lever is hardly used and we still have a room to go upwards. There is no point in correcting downwards or controlling price because we are fairly priced at this point of time

items.statement: Manufacturing shifting to outsourcing: currently 66% outsourced, 34% in-house; ratio to tilt further toward outsourcing.
items.quote: So, as we speak, we are about 66% outsourced and 34% in-house manufa cturing. Going forward as we know this ratio is still going to tilt in favor of

items.statement: Average selling price Rs 1,600 (mid-premium); average billing value Rs 3,620; annualized sales per sq ft Rs 16,048.
items.quote: The average sales price is ₹1,600. and the average bill ing value is ₹3,620, while our annualized sales per square foot stand at ₹16,048

items.statement: Management considers company too small to be impacted by macroeconomic challenges like inflation or supply-chain disruption.
items.quote: believe we are still at a nascent stage we should be worrying about economic challenges because there is nothing S D Retail Limited November 18, 2024 that we will be able to impact when there is an eco nomic challenge faced by the country. We are too small to bother about that at this point of time

items.statement: Proprietary software developed for POS data, customer data, replenishment, repeat buys, staff monitoring, store upkeep, fast-selling SKUs.
items.quote: we have recently developed proprietary software, which will collect a lot of d ata from point of sales including customer data, replenishment data, frequency of data, repeat buys and also towards the management efficiencies of the store in terms of monitoring of retail staff, cleanliness of the store, upkeeping of the store, fast selling skews, availab ility at the store

items.statement: Online channel growth now maturing; offline and online growing at similar single-digit rates.
items.quote: we have observed for last couple of years that this channel is also mature so now the growth of offline and online channel is almost simultaneou s with same single digit growth happening across channels

items.statement: Future category expansion limited to 8 PM-8 AM consumption occasions (e.g., loungewear) after sleepwear focus for 3-5 years.
items.quote: if you see the philosophy of the company is we are looking at consumption between 8 p.m. to 8 a.m., so any consumption story any consumption idea in this time zone which is 8 in the evening to 8 a.m. in the morning would naturally be an add-on category for us in future

items.statement: Textile volumes grew 14-15% QoQ and 17-18% YoY; health and hygiene volumes down 10-15% due to customer portfolio changes and monsoon seasonality
items.quote: From the demand point of view, we have done very well in textiles. There has been growth in the volume in textiles by almost 14% to 15% Q-o-Q basis. And in fact, Y-o-Y basis, there has been in fact, further growth of almost, I can say 17% to 18% in the textile division.

items.statement: Maintained EBITDA margin around 25% and gross margins 35-40% despite raw material and freight volatility
items.quote: But if you also see, we have been able to maintain our EBITDA margins, which is almost 25% even in this quarter. So, as such, we have been able to have more better product mix of speciality chemicals, sustainable product lines, which is helping us to add and deliver more value to the customer at the same time helping us to have healthy EBITDAs.

items.statement: Ambernath Phase 1 (18,000-20,000 tons) expected operational by beginning of next financial year (Q1 FY26); will shift some lines from Mahape plant
items.quote: So the first step would be to have the Phase 1, which will be around 18,000 to 20,000 tons. That is number one. And we are hopeful that by the beginning of the next financial year, it should be up.

items.statement: Ambernath 1 plant scaled from 20,000 to 61,000 tons in 3 years; new Phase 1 to add 18,000-20,000 tons initially with incremental expansion thereafter
items.quote: As you have also seen in our Ambernath 1 plant, which was started 3 years back, we have started with 20,000 tons and now it's 61,000 tons. And it is done beautifully within time, within cost parameters, and it has been done in a way where the expenses are very much controlled.

items.statement: Export share increased to ~30% from ~25% driven by textile chemical exports, Bangladesh recovery, Vietnam and Middle East participation
items.quote: So, as such, our exports have slightly increased. It is now almost 30% from our earlier was I think 25% to 24% or something like that. Anupam Agarwal: Okay. Sanjay Tibrewala: This has increased definitely. This is also because of the increase in the textile chemical exports, Bangladesh picking

items.statement: Raised INR 342.55 crores total this year (INR 218 crores latest tranche via preferential allotment and warrants); promoter contributed INR 45 crores
items.quote: Additionally, we have completed a successful fund-raise of INR 218 crores through preferential allotment of equity shares and commodity warrants, bringing our total fund-raise this year to INR 342.55 crores.

items.statement: Advanced discussions for acquisition; disciplined approach, funds ready, targeting fungible businesses with similar ROCE/ROE/EBITDA margins, not distressed assets
items.quote: See, as such, what's the maximum information I can give on this platform, It's something which we have already mentioned on the stock exchange also, that we are on an advanced stage of discussion with certain company and a lot of documentations and exchanges and due diligence and legal and finance, as you know, these things have to be well done.

items.statement: ICRA upgraded long-term fund-based cash credit rating to ICRA A+ with positive outlook; long-term and short-term unallocated ratings reaffirmed at ICRA A+ and ICRA A1+ with positive outlook
items.quote: We are also pleased to share that ICRA on 11th November upgraded its credit rating for Fineotex. The long-term fund-based cash credit rating has been upgraded to ICRA A+, with a positive outlook, while the long-term and short-term unallocated rating has been reaffirmed at ICRA A+, and ICRA A1+, with a positive outlook.

items.statement: ESOP 2020: 25,052 equity shares allotted; 110 employees now covered as of September 30
items.quote: Recently, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee approved the allotment of 25,052 equity shares through the Fineotex Chemical Limited ESOP 2020, with 110 employees now included for ESOP as of September 30.

items.statement: R&D spend steady at INR 7-8 crores annually; absolute spend rising while percentage of revenue declining due to 40% YoY growth
items.quote: As such, more or less, our outflow of R&D budget is almost INR 7 crores to INR 8 crores as we speak today.

items.statement: Offering full fabric guarantee packages with fixed pricing per kg/meter; brands approving Fineotex products and mandating use by their suppliers for consistency
items.quote: What we have started doing in the recent past also, I mean, we were doing it in the earlier days in a couple of quarters before, we initiated those time, but now things are picking up where we go and do the entire guarantee of the fabric for the customer from unfinished to finished, in which we can give a basket of a product, we give our own recipes.

items.statement: European competitors (Archroma etc.) facing same external headwinds (Bangladesh, freight, geopolitics); Fineotex gaining wallet share and geography with 250+ ZDHC/GOTS approved products vs 150-200 for multinationals
items.quote: Almost, I think we have crossed 250 products in that category itself, whereas, even if we compare to the likes of the European multinationals, they will not have more than 150 or 200. So, this also reinforced in the minds of the customers how technical company we are and how we are focused on our R&D and getting better than others, much ahead than others.

items.statement: Participated in ADIPEC (Abu Dhabi), OTC Houston, Vietnam, Bangladesh exhibitions; export share up to ~30%; dollar up ~2%; freight and container costs rising
items.quote: Last week, we were in ADIPEC also. This was the first time we have been participating in ADIPEC. This is the biggest exhibition and show, it happens in Abu Dhabi every year for the Middle East and other markets.

items.statement: Unprecedented volatility in freight, raw material prices and USD over last quarter (weekly swings vs normal 6-month trends) making procurement timing difficult; customers resistant to price increases
items.quote: However, this was the time when we are seeing fluctuations, like, one week, you start booking your products and raw materials. By the next week, you will see that it's gone up or it's gone down. So, it's very hard to predict the right time to do that. And obviously, the customers in most any markets will always be not ready to accept your -- the new prices or higher prices or whatever it is.

items.statement: FY25 H2 invoicing target: VFX INR 25-26 cr, branded content INR 20-22 cr, AI platforms INR 5 cr
items.quote: On the visual effects side. We're looking at on a very conservative level INR25 crores to INR26 crores worth of invoicing by March. On the branded content side, on a very conservative side, we're looking at around INR 20 crores of invoicing by March and on our platform, we're looking at an invoicing of around INR5 crores by March.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance revised to INR 125 cr; FY27 guidance INR 200 cr maintained
items.quote: The revised projections for FY26 is 125. Obviously, we are best, we take every endeavour to try to beat that as far as possible.

items.statement: VFX business pipeline of INR 56 cr over next 7-8 months; INR 25-26 cr expected invoicing by March
items.quote: Cumulatively, if I were to look at it which I have the numbers right in front of me, we have a business pipeline of approximately INR56 crores in visual effects to be delivered over the next 7 months to 8 months' time. And out of this, we are anticipating somewhere between INR 25 crores to INR28 crores to be invoiced by March.

items.statement: Branded content: 58 episodes deal with Jio Cinema worth INR 30 cr up to March 2024
items.quote: So we've signed up a deal for 58 episodes with Jio Cinema for up to March 24. So that is what that, and the total value of that is approximately INR30 crores.

items.statement: VFX industry returning to normalcy after Hollywood strikes; multiple projects starting Dec-Feb
items.quote: The visual effects industry is slowly creeping back to normalcy which is a great sign for us. We have started work on several projects. We have tons of projects in the horizon where we've received soft confirmation from our clients, some of them starting in December, some of them starting in January, some of them starting in February.

items.statement: Current blended PAT margin ~21%; expected to normalize to 18-20% as North America projects ramp up
items.quote: Our margins in the last 6 months have taken a hit because of this added cost in North America and these people don't come cheap. We are spending close to a little over a INR1.5 crores salaries in North America currently. With little more revenue out there, so that i s affecting our current margin, but as these projects begin, we normalize to our regular PAT margins which we've always anticipated o

items.statement: Receivables increased to INR 41 cr; majority of collections expected over next 4-6 months
items.quote: We do anticipate a majority of these collections to happen over the next 4 months to 6 months' time. This is something which we have been through once already post COVID.

items.statement: FY26 receivable days expected to improve 200% as revenue mix shifts to direct projects
items.quote: 200% because in FY26, while we had initially planned that FY26, 50% of our revenue will be outsourced and 50% direct. We anticipate more of it to be direct. The minute you go into the direct project and direct revenue league, your receivable days become much more co mfortable compared to

items.statement: North America hires (David, Jason, Marina, Tara) secured direct projects from Amazon, Netflix, Hulu, CBS including One Piece and Duffer Brothers show
items.quote: Out of this, if I'm just going to break this, I'm going to break this up into 14, maybe around INR16 crores worth of this INR56 crores from our existing clients, which are our outsource par tners, who outsource work to us a nd the remaining INR 41 crores-odd work that is going to be starting is all the efforts of Jason, David, and Marina. Because these are all direct projects from Amazon, from Hul

items.statement: Streaming platforms (Netflix, Amazon, Disney) cutting content spend for 2025; VFX volume expected to reduce
items.quote: We have seen trends which we've been learning as we progress that Netflix, Amazon, Disney, CDs, they are all cutting down on their projects a little. It's not the same way it was in 2022 or the early 2023 when average when Netflix was spending USD15 billion a year on content. As for the latest news figures that we've got and after speaking to some senior people at Netflix, they are all cutting dow

items.statement: Indian VFX tax rebate requires minimum INR 1.5 cr per project; applicable to direct projects like One Piece, Star Trek
items.quote: the Indian government has kept a rider out here that the project has to be a minimum value of INR 1.5 crores and only then you can apply for the tax rebate. In our outsourced work that we've been doing so far, it's rare that one proj ect is of this value. It does not work per client. This works per project. Now, when we start working directly on a One Piece or The Last of Us or the Star Trek serie

items.statement: Zero attrition in last 4 months due to industry job scarcity; hiring to ramp up Dec-Jan as projects commence
items.quote: Ma'am the last 4 months, I'm proud to tell you, we had literally zero attrition because here people don't have jobs in the industry. So anybody who has a job, it's worth its weight in gold. Nobody's leaving right now, but yes once hiring starts December, January there will be attrition.

items.statement: No acquisition plans currently; no VFX studio with intrinsic value (captive clients/tech) identified
items.quote: Yes, so we don't have any acquisition plans in the immediate horizon. I believe that acquisition when you acquire something, there should be intrinsic value in that, in terms of either captive clients or technology. We don't foresee any VFX studio right now who is worth acquiring, who brings in intrinsic value.

items.statement: Thanksgiving-Christmas slowdown may delay collections till December end; faster recovery expected from January
items.quote: We are actually in a very precarious time of the year, unfortunately, which is the truth that we all have to live with. Thanksgiving, I don't know if any of you have been to the US market or European market. After Thanksgiving, it's like a vacation period for the American markets. The Thanksgiving is now it will be next week. Once Thanksgiving is done and then they get into Christmas, New Year mod

items.statement: Targets Rs 500 crore revenue for FY25 with EBITDA margin of 9.5-10.5%
items.quote: Our current running order book is Rs. 126 crores and we are confident to achieving a new milestone of our Rs. 500 crores revenue target this financial year.

items.statement: Expects FY26 revenue of around Rs 650 crore with new projects contributing
items.quote: Yes, we are expecting somewhere in the range of around Rs. 650 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 9.5-10.5% for FY25 and going forward
items.quote: our focus is to maintain around 9.5% to 10.5% EBITDA going forward with around 25% to 30% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Current order book at Rs 136+ crore as of call date
items.quote: the numbers of orders we are having as on today is Rs. 136 plus crores

items.statement: Received orders from West Bengal Livestock (Rs 9.63 cr), NEDB Himachal (Rs 8.28 cr), J&K Horticulture (Rs ~10 cr)
items.quote: We have received one order from the Dairy Modernization for the Rs. 9.63 crores as well as from the NEDB for the Refrigeration Plant in Himachal Pradesh of valued up Rs. 8.28 crores and from Jammu and Kashmir Horticulture Board for the CA Cold Storage of about Rs. 10 crores

items.statement: Phase 1 capex of Rs 100 crore nearly complete; Continuous PUF Panel Rs 64 cr, Commercial Freezer Rs 15 cr machinery arrived
items.quote: Our first phase in which we say that Rs. 100 crores CAPEX will be done in which if we add both Continuous Panel and Commercial Freezers then we can see that CAPEX as of now is at end

items.statement: Chennai plant (Bharat Refrigeration) civil work underway, completion by April 2025, shift by Q2 FY26, Rs 4.5-5 cr spent so far
items.quote: by April 25, it is likely to be completed and we will be able to shift that unit by 2nd Quarter of FY26

items.statement: Commercial Freezer plant capacity 1.25 lakh units/annum (8k Visi Coolers, rest Chest Freezers)
items.quote: our manufacturing capacity is 1.25 lakh per annum

items.statement: Continuous PUF Panel plant trial run done, production started this month; Commercial Freezer commissioning ongoing, production by month-end
items.quote: Continuous Panel production has started, this month we are expecting billing will be done. Commercial Freezers commissioning is going on and by the end of this month production will also start in that.

items.statement: E-commerce/quick commerce opportunity estimated at Rs 600 crore market over 2-3 years; currently 5-8% of revenue
items.quote: according to our projection, every Company is saying that we will make 2,000 dark stores and their existing numbers are around 300, 200, so I think that in the next 2 years, 3 years we can assume a total market of Rs. 600 crores from this.

items.statement: Cold Chain market projected to grow from $10.3B to $13.58B by 2029 at 5.67% CAGR
items.quote: Indian Cold Chain Storage and Logistic market is poised for significant growth as per the one of the recent report project a compound annual growth rate of 5.67% with a market size expected to expand from $10.30 US billion in 2024 to $13.58 US billion by 2029.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: Cold Rooms 48%, Commercial 17%, Transport 8%, Ammonia+Projects 23%, Industrial 4%
items.quote: In Cold Rooms we have done a business of 48%, Industrial Refrigeration's contribution is around 4%, Commercial is 17%, Van I am telling about Transport Refrigeration in that the contribution is around 8% and by combining both Ammonia and Project the contribution is 23%.

items.statement: FY25 expected mix: Cold Room 42-45%, Commercial 17%, Industrial 3%, Transport 7-9%, Ammonia 18-22%, New projects 10-12%
items.quote: We think that this year the Commercial vertical will be somewhere in the range of 17%. Cold Room vertical will be in the range of 42% to 45%. Industrial vertical will be around 3%. Transport Refrigeration will be in the range of 7% to 9%. Ammonia Vertical will be in the range of 18% to 22% and the business which we will do with our new projects that will be somewhere in the range of around 10% to

items.statement: Q2 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin 8.37% (up from 7.56% Q1, down from 10.11% YoY) due to new project manpower costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to 8.37% higher than 7.56% in Q1 FY25 although a slight below the 10.11% recorded in Q2 FY24 due to increase in strategic man power cost of our new project.

items.statement: New project gross margins: Continuous Panel 15-16%, Commercial Freezer 17-22%; EBITDA impact neutral due to low labor cost
items.quote: In Continuous Panel the gross margin is around 15%, 16% and in Commercial Freezer it is around 17% to 22%, it depend on volume with whom we are doing, so gross margins of 18% to 22% will be there. But labor cost is very less, so on EBITDA margin our existing EBITDA will complement it. There will be no compression.

items.statement: Management prioritizes revenue growth over margin expansion until Rs 2,000-3,000 crore topline achieved
items.quote: Until a sizeable topline of Rs. 2,000 or Rs. 3,000 is not achieved our focus will be not to focus on margins. You can see that in the last financial year the margin was somewhere in the range of about 11% at that time also we got a lot of questions like will you focus on margins, but at that time also we told that right now our margin is not our focus, to increase our margins is not our focus.

items.statement: No discounting needed vs larger competitors; pricing at par based on after-sales service and customization
items.quote: We don't need to get orders by giving discounts.

items.statement: Receivables spike in September due to Rs 23-24 cr project payments; Rs 14 cr collected in following weeks; annual working capital turnover target 6x
items.quote: We can expect an annual working capital turnover of 6x.

items.statement: Long-term debt capped at current Rs 65 crore level; working capital limit enhanced to Rs 65 crore (Rs 40 cr fund-based + Rs 25 cr extra), ~50% utilization
items.quote: The long-term debt which we currently have I don't think that it will increase anymore. It is possible that due to undertaking of small tools may be one or more small loans can come, but still the long-term debt will not go beyond the current level of Rs. 65 crores in next year.

items.statement: Working with all major e-commerce players (Flipkart, new entrants); existing relationships with most Indian ice cream/frozen food manufacturers
items.quote: Actually in E-commerce we work with all the good and big players, the new people who are coming like brokers and dialogues are going on with old ones like Flipkart

items.statement: Addressable market expands from Rs 6,000 cr to Rs 15,000 cr with new products (Continuous Panel Rs 4,000 cr, Commercial Freezer Rs 3,000-4,000 cr)
items.quote: If we add our new product that is our Commercial Freezer as well as the Continuous Freezers it will be total Rs. 15,000 crores in all

items.statement: Data center cooling opportunity evaluated but not pursued due to mismatch with refrigeration expertise
items.quote: it is purely air-condition business and we are refrigeration people that is why that opportunity doesn't fit in our existing Product Manufacturing and Instrumentation skill that is why we cannot get any benefit from that.

items.statement: Promoter pledged 4.15% shares for personal home loan (2-3 year tenure), not for capex
items.quote: It was for my personal home loan. The loan was for my home that is why I have pledged it. Maybe it is for the time period of 2 years, 3 years.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of Rs 300-400 crore
items.quote: Fair projection right now seems is 300 to 400 crores between somewhere and if something additional comes out, which is in pipeline, because mostly the government tenders and things are there, unless they are awarded and we start the work, we cannot depend on that.

items.statement: FY25 PAT margin guidance of around 10%
items.quote: For the entire year. I think it's a fair estimate. It will be slightly higher than that, but 10% is the estimate that is which I stick to.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 10-12%
items.quote: It will be 10% definitely, it can be 11%, it can be 12% also.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of Rs 1,000 crore
items.quote: We will definitely reach 300 crores plus. 400 crores is something because of two elections and then monsoon and all those things. So, I am a little bit skeptical. I will try to reach there.

items.statement: New 700 km order pending election results, expected to add to FY25 and FY26 revenue
items.quote: It is still on the table. We have to wait till this election result on 23 rd. Maybe by 25th or so I will get the things cleared. We wait for another 15-days, but it is positive

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 11.85%, Q2 FY25 at 8.32% due to monsoon seasonality
items.quote: Our total income surged to 91.82 crores, reflective impressive year -on-year growth of 511.35%, EBITDA stood to 10.88 crores, making a 145.78% increase, with an EBITDA margin of 11.85%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 margin compression due to inventory build-up for new project execution
items.quote: See, new project has started, inventory has built up, because every day we do three to four kilometers of trenching and ducting. For that I have to have stock for at least one month.

items.statement: Vodafone impact limited to 15-20% of telecom revenue (~6% of total); diversified across telecom and infrastructure
items.quote: Sir, that will have real impact of about 15% on the telecom revenue. That is why we have diversified into infrastructure and telecom, both. So, even if one side goes weak, then we can recover from the other.

items.statement: Additional machines purchased for Samruddhi Highway road work
items.quote: Machines are purchased already.

items.statement: Added three managers and two supervisors for Samruddhi project; senior telecom consultants engaged
items.quote: Yes, we have got the three-manager level and two supervisor level additions. They are being briefed and trained for the Samruddhi project and we are going to take additional couple of people because this is very long.

items.statement: Additional funds needed; will approach after pending tenders are awarded
items.quote: Additional funds, definitely we need. I am waiting for one more tender to be realized, then I can justify the need, and I will definitely come. We will need additional funds.

items.statement: H1 FY25 total income Rs 91.82 crore, up 511% YoY; EBITDA Rs 10.88 crore, up 146%; PAT Rs 7.58 crore, up 142%
items.quote: Our total income surged to 91.82 crores, reflective impressive year -on-year growth of 511.35%, EBITDA stood to 10.88 crores, making a 145.78% increase, with an EBITDA margin of 11.85%, net profit for the period grew significantly to 7.58 crores representing year -on-year growth of 142.44%.

items.statement: Will accept lower margins (concessions) to achieve Rs 1,000 crore revenue scale
items.quote: When we move to 1,000 crores, the profit margin will be slightly lower, because when volumes increase, profits decrease. To reach there, I will have to make some concessions.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase-III avoided due to low margins and litigation; focus on quality EPC contracts
items.quote: About BharatNet, anyway, we don't operate on that. BharatNet is always sarkari. I will not comment more. BharatNet is a very low margin business.

items.statement: Exploring defense/deep tech via DRDO/IIT incubation; new mixed revenue streams to be announced in December
items.quote: We have already approached DRDO through IIT where we have won incubation. My son's company is there, and presentations and things are done. Soon, we will get the call from concerned people.

items.statement: Accounting treatment of work-in-progress under review after investor feedback on quarterly margin distortion
items.quote: Let me discuss with my chartered accountant please. He's with me right now. Your suggestion is accepted. We will look into it. Next time you will see accounting in a slightly different way.

items.statement: Management reiterated 25% CAGR guidance over FY22-FY27 period, not necessarily 25% every year
items.quote: We will try our best. So, what we have always given a guidance is that in the 5-year period, average CAGR growth will be 25%.

items.statement: Total capex program of Rs 4,500 crores by FY27, approximately 50% complete or in progress
items.quote: Out of the total capital expenditure program of Rs. 4,500 crores by FY27, approximately already 50% is complete and or currently in progress

items.statement: New Mumbai liquid terminal of ~150,000 kL planned with estimated project cost of Rs 250 crores on leased port land
items.quote: We plan to build a storage terminal with capacity of approximately 150,000 kL on this site with an estimated project cost of around Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: LPG storage capacity to increase by 130,000 MT by end FY25 via New Mangalore and Pipavav expansions
items.quote: Our ongoing capacity expansion at New Mangalore in Karnataka and Pipavav in Gujarat is expected to increase our LPG storage capacity by 130,000 metric tonnes by the end of fiscal 2025.

items.statement: JNPT greenfield liquid expansion of ~101,900 cubic meters almost complete, partial commissioning expected by next call
items.quote: In the liquid division, our ongoing greenfield expansion at JNPT in Navi Mumbai aims to increase our storage capacity by about 101,900 cubic meters, almost complete.

items.statement: Liquid capacity expansions: JNPT ~100,000 kL, Mangalore ~71,000 kL, Kandla ~25,000 kL, Mumbai 150,000 kL (yet to begin)
items.quote: The expansion is in JNPT, which is 100,000 approximately. There is 71,000 odd in Mangalore, 25,000 odd in Kandla. And Mumbai we have just said 150,000 is yet to begin.

items.statement: Ammonia terminal of 25,000 MT capacity at Pipavav in JV, anchor customer committed, construction to start after permits
items.quote: We had announced the capacity expansion at our first ammonia terminal of 25,000 metric tonnes capacity, which will be located in the state of Gujarat.

items.statement: Pipavav and Mangalore LPG projects to be commissioned soon with revenue expected from Q1 FY26

items.quote: No, I don't want to revise that I want to stay there what I anticipated, and we are going to be delivering that basically.

items.quote: So, we are looking close to a good numbers are going to come and growth rate, we are looking to be a 20% to 25% on an auto and auto component machines also to be there in the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: INR110 crore spent on semiconductor facility so far; total project INR140 crore; INR30-35 crore more in FY26
items.quote: Well, as of today, we have incurred an expenditure of about INR110 crores. The project size that we had submitted to Ministry of Electronics and IT, it was INR140 crores. So, as we go along, we will be investing another INR30-odd crores in the next financial year.

items.statement: Planning INR200 crore investment under ISM 2.0 scheme with 50% capex subsidy for advanced packaging
items.quote: So, under that scheme, we are envisaging to invest INR200 crores, whereby 50% of that investment will come as a capex subsidy from the government.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization ~55% at SEZ Noida; new Bhiwadi facility for high-volume domestic business
items.quote: The capacity that we have currently at 55% is primarily at the existing unit at the SEZ in Noida. The new capacity that we're building up at our new facility in Biharwadi is primarily to cater to large-volume business and also the domestic sector as well.

items.statement: Two sizable contracts signed in Taiwan and Dubai; exploring EU, UK, Middle East, Southeast Asia
items.quote: Two sizable contracts, one in Taiwan and the other in Dubai, have been signed. Other geographies like the European Union, UK, Middle East, and Southeast Asia are being explored to ensure a stronger pipeline of orders.

items.statement: InnoCare MoU signed for flat panel detection device; $3-4 million revenue potential; commercial revenue from FY26
items.quote: And also, having said that, the revenue potential over a period of time is anywhere between $3 million to $4 million.

items.statement: Semiconductor focus: LED drivers (legacy packaging), DFN packages (security), NAND flash/EMMC/BGA (advanced); EMS: medical, marine, automotive, metering
items.quote: One is the memory chips. The other one is this commodity chips like LED drivers. And the third that we are looking at is industrial applications of RFID and DFN packages that Varun Manwani spoke about.

items.statement: Actively pursuing new OEM partnerships for IT hardware (local and global brands) to replace Thomson; new EMS customers added across sectors
items.quote: We are in discussions with local and global OEMs and brands. And they are looking at the Indian market. Some of them are existing players, some of them are players who have business worldwide, but are also looking to enter into India or let's say restart things in India as well.

items.statement: Government import restrictions on IT hardware driving deal finalization; PLI for IT hardware (4-8%) and SPEC/ISM schemes for semiconductors (25% then 50% capex subsidy)
items.quote: And this is a very positive step from the government because it pushes the brands and the IT hardware community to hasten their deal signing.

items.statement: ~80% revenue from exports; ~75% of exports from US; diversifying to Taiwan, Dubai, EU, UK, Middle East, Southeast Asia
items.quote: What we are saying is that 80% of our turnover is from exports and within exports bulk of it about 75% is from the US.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used to reduce working capital requirements; INR7 crore sales in transit due to SEZ invoice approval delays
items.quote: Towards the end of the month, we did raise an invoice for about INR7 crores to a few customers. But because of the regulations in SEZ, the customers had to approve the invoice.

items.statement: No specific debt discussion; IPO proceeds deployed for stake increase, working capital, equipment; INR100 crore FD held per prospectus
items.quote: From the IPO proceeds, about INR40 crores has been utilized for increasing our stake in our Semicon subsidiary, and some proceeds have been also used to bring down our working capital requirements as well as for some equipment purchase.

items.statement: Increased stake in Sahasra Semiconductor from 54% to 72.7% using IPO proceeds; targeting full control in FY25
items.quote: We have already invested after IPO. We have increased our shareholding in semiconductor to 72.7%. And within this financial year, we hope to increase it significantly so that we have such a semiconductor in complete control of your company.

items.statement: No M&A discussed; focus on organic growth and JV (Infopower with MiTac) in Tegna EMC cluster
items.quote: There are five investors, including Foxling, Oppo, Winbond, and also one of our group companies, Infopower, where we have joint venture with MiTac.

items.statement: Senior expat hire Jerry Enriquez (ex-TI, On Semi) for semiconductor manufacturing; more expat hires planned
items.quote: We have made a Senior Expat hire for our semiconductor units. Mr. Jerry Enriquez from the Philippines have joined us recently and come with a rich experience of 18 years from organizations like Texas Instruments and On Semi.

items.statement: Semiconductor demand to double globally to $1T in 6 years; India semiconductor market to grow 6x; India electronics demand to 4x to $400B
items.quote: Further to what has been discussed, semiconductor demand worldwide will double in the next six years, and it is expected to move from the current demand of about $500 billion to over $1 trillion. The semiconductor landscape in India is expected to grow six-fold in the same period.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility impacted US export orders in H1; US-China trade tensions seen as positive for India; Thomson partnership underperforming
items.quote: Geopolitical volatility across the world has had an impact on export orders from the US in the first half of this year. Your company sees stability going forward, and the new administration in the US may impact positively to our growth.

items.statement: R&D spend ~1-1.5% of revenue; designing Intel-chipset motherboard for Make in India; LED driver chip design to be internalized
items.quote: Well, as we go along, we intend to spend somewhere around 1% to 1.5% at least of the revenue in our R&D.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth expected in line with H1 FY25 growth of 13.8% constant currency; EBITDA margins to stay steady at current levels
items.quote: We expect the growth for the full-year ending March 25, to be in line with our growth performance in H1, and our EBITDA margins to stay steady at these levels for the full year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue grew 19.8% YoY constant currency driven by existing client demand and new logo wins
items.quote: Our growth, like I said, like in the past, our growth was led by demand from our existing clients and our new logo wins.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin at 25.5%, up YoY from consistent 24-25% range, driven by operational efficiencies and lower corporate costs
items.quote: This reflects an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.5%. Our adjusted EBITDA margin has been very healthy. Like I said, historically, we've maintained very consistent margins.

items.statement: Top 5 clients average tenure 17 years; still only cover ~80% of service portfolio per client, leaving white space for wallet share expansion
items.quote: for the same client, even for our top client, we probably only do, roughly about 80% of the service portfolio that I've shown, right? So there is still opportunity for us t o work with each of these clients in areas which we are not supporting them today on

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex spend was ₹682 million
items.quote: CapEx spend during the first half of the year was ₹682 million.

items.statement: Headcount increased by 2,522 in Q2 to 38,380 total; 94% offshore/nearshore; annualised attrition stable at 25.8%
items.quote: So the overall headcount, at the end of the second qu arter stood at about 38,380. Our annualised attrition is very stable at 25.8

items.statement: DSOs at end of Q2 FY25 stood at 72.5 days; H1 operating cash flow 114% of reported EBITDA
items.quote: The DSOs at the end of the quarter stood at 72.5 days. Our strong operational performance resulted in a very strong free cash flow of 101% to EBITDA.

items.statement: Net debt including leases 0.78x TTM EBITDA, excluding leases 0.34x; FY25 net debt guided at ₹8,020 million, FY26 at ₹5,670 million with repayments of ₹2,490m and ₹2,350m respectively
items.quote: As of FY '25, we are likely to have ₹8020 million. And for FY '26, it will be ₹5,670 million. We'd be repaying about ₹2,490 million in FY '25, ₹2,350 million in the next year.

items.statement: Payer vertical 89.2% of revenue (grew 20.8% YoY), Provider 10.8% (grew 23.7% YoY); clinical services and payment integrity identified as fast-growing areas
items.quote: During the quarter, our Payer vertical grew 20.8% year-on-year and contributed to 89.2% on the revenue mix. And the Provider vertical grew 23.7% and contributed to 10.8% of the total revenues.

items.statement: Compete with Cognizant, Accenture in some payer deals; differentiation is deeper domain expertise and ability to run GenAI pilots within existing operations
items.quote: we do come across people like, Cognizant, Accenture in some of our Payer opportunities. But not all of the Indian IT service pl ayers, do we see in those opportunities

items.statement: No major risk seen from US policy changes; revenue is non-discretionary core operations spend; diversified across commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, exchange segments
items.quote: The kind of work that we do, our work for our clients, and I forgot to point this out is the revenues that we make is part of the non-discretionary spend, right? Because we run core operations for our clients.

items.statement: Captive sourcing by US payers is a risk; some large captives belong to non-clients, but existing clients also discuss setting up captives for core operations
items.quote: A number of them are now thinking about setting up captives for core operations, which is what we do for them, right? So I mean, these conversations come up every now and then even with the existing clients.

items.statement: US healthcare outsourcing penetration only ~20% of $200B core operational spend, leaving large runway for wallet share gains and market penetration
items.quote: If you look at the total outsourcing penetration, it's still in the 20s. So there is still a large part of the work that clients still tend to do in-house.

items.statement: M&A is a key lever: capability acquisitions like BirchAI and DCI; actively seeking mid-market client access acquisitions
items.quote: M&A is a key lever for us to build our capability. So we're looking at two kinds of M&A's. One is, capability-based acquisitions, just like a BirchAI or a DCI. And we are also constantly looking for other opportunities, which will give us access to a much larger pool of clients.

items.statement: GenAI pilots running across front office, back office, clinical; expect 15-20% of interactions automatable but larger efficiency gains via knowledge retrieval and summarisation
items.quote: We don't see a full automation, beyond 15%, 20%. But having said that, we think there is a tremendous opportunity to improve the efficiency, right?

items.statement: Management aims for low-to-mid teens revenue growth, consistent with historical trend, and targets 8-12 new client additions per year.
items.quote: we've always grown in double-digits. We've grown, I would say in the low teens to mid -teens number. And th at's a number that you see us growing this year as well

items.statement: Top five client revenue concentration target is 60-65% over the next two to three years, down from current 80%.
items.quote: But, yeah, in the next, if you're giving me a two, three year time frame, we want the top five clients from t he 80% to come down somewhere between 60% to 65

items.statement: Mid-market outsourcing penetration is very low (single digits), creating white space; large payers have 40%+ penetration.
items.quote: The large guys would have done a lit tle more. They'll probably have a 40% plus, 25 penetration. Whereas the smaller guys may be in the single-digits

items.statement: New client wins in mid-market are mostly greenfield (first-time outsourcers); large client wins come as additional vendor or in new clinical areas.
items.quote: The outsourcing penetration in the mid and small space is very, very small. So if I'm winning opportunities in the mid-market, it is very likely that the client hasn't outsourced at all, so it's a white space from an outsourcing point of view.

items.statement: Provider side growing marginally faster than Payer but remains ~10% of revenue; clinical programs and payment integrity are key differentiators vs India TPAs.
items.quote: Even today, the Provider is growing marginally faster than the Payer of business. But we are constantly looking to grow that faster, because our Provider portfolio compared to the Pa yer is a lot more restricted

items.statement: Investing in market-facing team and technology (GenAI pilots for knowledge retrieval, summarization) to drive efficiency and support BPaaS model for larger deal sizes.
items.quote: we are in the process of trying that ou t, it's early days. But if we execute on that strategy successfully, then we believe that the deal sizes can be much larger and the growth rate can be higher than what it is

items.statement: Only 2-3 players (Accenture, Cognizant) have larger healthcare operations revenues (~$1B annually); high domain expertise creates strong entry barriers.
items.quote: We believe that some of the bigger players like Accenture and Cognizant, their revenues could be closer to the 1 billion mark annually. So but, there wouldn't be more than two or three folks who would have larger revenues than us in the space we are in.

items.statement: US healthcare administrative system is unique; clinical capabilities are globally replicable but near-term focus remains on US market due to size and opportunity.
items.quote: The admini strative system of the U.S. healthcare is very different than what you would encounter in other places. But the clinical side, whatever we are doing is equally applicable, right

items.statement: Over 90% of revenue is recurring (operational services); contracts typically 3 years; payment models include FTE, transaction, PMPM, and contingency.
items.quote: At a high level, everything that we do, like I said I would say over 90% of the work that we do is operational services, which is a recurring revenue.
